articles.title: Account security and passkeys
articles.description: Admin → Settings → Security
articles.body: Admin → Settings → Security Add a passkey Open security settings on a compatible browser and register a passkey using the device prompt. Verify it appears in your account list. Sign in with a passkey Use the passkey sign-in option and complete the browser/device verification. A device unlock does not grant restaurant permissions you do not already hold. Remove an unused key Select an unused passkey in security settings and confirm removal. Keep a working sign-in method before removing your last key. If the operation fails If the device prompt fails, keep the existing key and use another configured sign-in method.

articles.title: Subscription and billing status
articles.description: Admin → Account → Billing, when offered
articles.body: Admin → Account → Billing, when offered Read the current subscription Check the recorded plan, subscription status and relevant trial/renewal/grace date. Confirm commercial terms with Foody; technical plan labels can differ from current offers. Review a plan change An authorized owner reviews and confirms an offered plan change. Wait for the subscription reread; if uncertain, verify the recorded plan before submitting again. Review billing events Inspect event type, date, amount and currency. Contact support for an unexplained failed payment or blocked subscription; an order payment is separate from the software subscription.

articles.title: Restaurant business assistant
articles.description: Open the AI business panel in Admin with an authorized restaurant account. This panel is distinct from the public help assistant.
articles.body: Open the AI business panel in Admin with an authorized restaurant account. This panel is distinct from the public help assistant. Ask about business data Choose the intended restaurant and ask a precise question about current/weekly sales, top items, stock, recent orders, customers, staff or menu. Review the answer against the relevant source screen. AI interpretation is not proof of payment reconciliation or a substitute for accounting. Understand the panel’s scope Available business queries use the signed-in restaurant context. The public support assistant receives only published guides and conversation. Do not paste business/customer exports, passwords or card details into public support. If a business answer is unsupported, use the source module or contact an authorized manager.

articles.title: Read your dashboard and reports
articles.description: Choose the date basis and understand which orders are counted.
articles.body: Open the corresponding Foody workspace described below. Read paid-order discounts In the POS sales report, Discounts (paid orders) includes only discounts on paid orders in the period. Gross sales follows the dashboard’s counting rule, which may also include accepted unpaid orders. Do not subtract these cards to derive a net: net sales, refunds and fees remain unavailable here. Read sales on the POS With analytics.view, open More → Reports → Sales. On a tablet the left rail keeps the permitted sections available; on a phone open them from Reports. Choose Today, Week, Month, Quarter or Year. Each calendar period starts at its beginning and ends today; the week starts on Monday. The reference day comes from the restaurant, not the phone clock. The report uses the current restaurant, order creation dates and the dashboard’s configured counted-order rule. Amounts alone therefore do not prove bank collection. Refresh reloads the period without recording a payment. Review gross sales, sale count, average sale, discounts, the chart and recorded payment methods. Expand an item for its actual variants or a category for its items. Items and categories use paid lines with combo attribution; delivery and discounts can explain differences from order totals. A dash for net sales, refunds or fees means that metric is not supplied for the period, not that it is zero. Refresh a failed load rather than treating it as a day without sales. This report closes neither physical cash nor a Verifone card batch. Start from Home Open Home in FoodyAdmin. The dashboard shows the selected period or service, the orders requiring attention, gross sales, order count, average order value, items sold and recent orders. What you can open depends on your permissions. Check the date basis The date control can use order dates or a scheduled service/series. A future service can include orders already placed for that service: those figures do not mean that service has been completed. Check the date basis before comparing figures with another report. The orders counted control indicates the revenue calculation, such as paid orders or accepted orders. Accepted-order sales are not proof that all payments were collected. Review payment attention separately. Comparisons and unavailable data Comparisons depend on an available previous period or service. For a future or ongoing service, the dashboard explains why a comparison is not shown. Unavailable data and an empty period are different; use Refresh or resolve the reported load error before interpreting missing figures as zero. Detailed reports Open Reports for the reporting pages your role permits. Select the date range and review the applied filters. The overview provides an export action; export the selected scope and check that its dates and calculation match your intended analysis. Open the current weekly batch automatically For a restaurant configured for weekly batches, open Home or Orders using the Série date basis. The current batch is selected by default even without orders; its totals then stay at zero. It advances after the previous batch’s final fulfillment day in the restaurant timezone, without waiting for the first order or for ordering to open. An open page follows this change on the next automatic refresh (about one minute) or when you return to the tab. You can select an older service in the calendar; that selection stays in place while the page is open. An order for a later week does not replace the current batch as the default. A payment-attention link keeps its explicit period. If the date looks incorrect, check the configured fulfillment days and restaurant timezone, then reload. Rollover does not create an order or publish a menu.

articles.title: Catering branches and routing
articles.description: Open Catering → Branches and Routing.
articles.body: Open Catering → Branches and Routing. Maintain eligible branches Create or edit the branch’s available fields and active state. Check its restaurant ownership and service associations. An inactive branch should not be used as a new customer destination. Set routing rules Create/edit a rule using the offered service, destination and conditions. Review priority/order and conflicts before saving. Check a representative request against the rules, and confirm before deleting a rule that existing workflows rely on.

articles.title: Catering events and balance collection
articles.description: Open Catering → Events and the intended event.
articles.body: Open Catering → Events and the intended event. Review the accepted event Check date/time, branch, guests, configuration, status and recorded payments. Use the available event actions only after checking production needs and assignments. Quote approval, event progress and payment status are distinct. Manage a supported balance authorization Open the balance panel and read its current state. Create/share a link or settle only when the displayed action is allowed by the provider and event state. Refresh/reconcile an ambiguous authorization before another operation. Do not treat an authorization as captured money.

articles.title: Catering questions, scheduling and pricing
articles.description: In the service editor open customer flow and pricing. Use the simulator before publishing.
articles.body: In the service editor open customer flow and pricing. Use the simulator before publishing. Configure customer steps Maintain step order, required questions and single-choice options. Configure scheduling, guest count, event details and selections supported by the service. Check translated labels and every branch of the flow; changing a question can affect pricing conditions. Maintain pricing rules Choose the item, base/fallback rate and conditional rules such as guest count, weekday, slot or a selected answer. Avoid overlapping specific rules. In the simulator choose a representative context and inspect the resolved rate and any conflict warning before saving.

articles.title: Review catering quotes
articles.description: Open Catering → Quotes and select the request. Review its current status and full configuration.
articles.body: Open Catering → Quotes and select the request. Review its current status and full configuration. Approve or reject a quote Check customer request, event date, guests, selections, calculated total and deposit status. If permitted adjust the total and add a note, then approve or reject explicitly. Confirm the saved status; a request awaiting review is not an accepted event. Review deposit and refund evidence Distinguish the primary deposit from a recorded duplicate charge. If Refund is available, select the intended target and amount and confirm once. For an external refund, first complete it in the provider console, then record its required reference in Foody. Recording an external refund does not itself move money. An uncertain provider result requires review before retrying.

articles.title: Catering services, catalog and offers
articles.description: Open Catering → Services, choose a service and its catalog/offer panels.
articles.body: Open Catering → Services, choose a service and its catalog/offer panels. Create and activate a service Create the service with name, description, slug and available languages, then review active state, quote mode and deposit policy. Save before adding its public page. An active service still needs the appropriate public configuration and availability. Maintain groups and items Add service catalog groups and items, edit descriptions, images/gallery, active state and pricing data. Review allowed selections and portion/guest quantities. This catering catalog is separate from ordinary POS menu groups; verify the service context before editing. Build offers and formulas Create/edit the service offer, its included items and choice constraints. Preview the configured customer flow and total. Do not publish an offer until all selectable items, quantities and required choices have been checked.

articles.title: Chains and branch management
articles.description: Open Chain/Branches or the chain dashboard with an authorized account.
articles.body: Open Chain/Branches or the chain dashboard with an authorized account. Choose the right branch Select the chain and branch, then verify the active restaurant context before editing menu, stock, staff or payments. Shared chain presentation does not make restaurant records interchangeable. Review public branch presence Maintain branch information and available website/ordering presence, then check the chain selector and branch destination. Confirm active menus, hours, fulfillment and payment configuration independently for each restaurant before publication.

articles.title: Message templates and workflow automation
articles.description: Open Settings → Message templates, WhatsApp templates or Order workflow according to the channel.
articles.body: Open Settings → Message templates, WhatsApp templates or Order workflow according to the channel. Create and review a template Edit supported localized text and variables, or submit a WhatsApp Utility template through the supported provider. Check approval, language and the positional variable contract before selection. Deleting a referenced template can be blocked even when its workflow stage is disabled. Attach messages to workflow stages Select an approved template on the intended stage and choose its supported timing. Stage-entry messages apply to future entries, not historical orders. Delivery reminders need saved delivery/courier data; satisfaction messages require recorded fulfillment. Read the selected trigger rather than assuming every reminder is sent the day before. Assign the file to a notification After approval, open Configure on the WhatsApp message, or Notify customer in Settings → Restaurant → Order workflow. Choose the photo/PDF model and then its fixed file from this restaurant’s library, or Receipt for this order for a PDF model. Save the page or workflow; Done only closes the general-message configuration panel. The workflow’s selected trigger and timing remain authoritative. Foody generates the receipt from the saved items and amounts for that order; it does not replace a tax invoice. Review the message and file previews before a manual send. Each message has one attachment, using activated direct Meta routing; these controls do not configure Twilio attachments. Review a route-based delivery reminder For an assigned delivery with a saved customer-window setting, reminders use the route arrival plus the configured duration, rather than the order’s broad scheduled slot. For example, arrival at 08:30 and 90 minutes produces 08:30–10:00. Configure it in Orders → Deliveries → allocation, beside the time at each stop, and review the manual or approved WhatsApp preview before sending. The same range supplies Twilio, Meta and stage reminders; existing template variables and J-1 eligibility remain in effect. Unconfigured historic routes keep the original saved slot. If the range cannot be verified, recalculate the route and reopen the reminder. A changed approved preview must be reviewed again before sending. Editing a template alone does not calculate a route or change its margin. Choose how to send a reminder Approved WhatsApp reminders can be previewed early, while manual buttons remain blocked until the day before delivery in the restaurant’s timezone. Orders → Deliveries → WhatsApp reminders reviews and confirms reminders across every route on the selected date; WhatsApp customer and Send this reminder handle one customer. Messages use the saved route’s calculated arrival window and assigned courier. Manual buttons use the global reminder template; automatic stages retain their explicitly configured template and timing in Order workflow. For day-before-only sending, select that timing on the intended stage, for example Ready. Opening a preview enables no trigger. A previously submitted, uncertain or failed reminder is never sent again by another mode, even if its text or provider changes. Changes before sending require a refreshed preview. Acceptance does not prove delivery; consult Customer messages on the order. Preview text represents the current calculation, not an earlier stored message. Automatically retrieve the Meta template image Prerequisite: an approved Utility template with a Photo header in the connected Meta account. In Settings → Communications → WhatsApp, open Configure for the message: Foody reloads the templates and automatically retrieves their Meta image. The preview displays the image above the text without uploading a file to Foody. An existing selection without a file also follows the Meta image. If you previously selected a local image, choose Image from Meta template under Photo, then Done and Save to use Meta’s image. Explicit local file selections are preserved. Refresh templates and connection reloads edits made in Meta. Satisfaction and workflow-stage previews also use this image; the order composer displays the actual attachment. The image must be a JPEG/PNG accessible from Meta, up to 5 MB. If retrieval fails, the preview offers Refresh and sending fails without a text-only fallback. Check the image in Meta if its link is unavailable. An image changed after a manual send was prepared requires a new preview before sending. Opening and refreshing never sends a message.

articles.title: Connect and operate WhatsApp
articles.description: Open Settings → WhatsApp. Select the supported connection/billing mode before entering credentials.
articles.body: Open Settings → WhatsApp. Select the supported connection/billing mode before entering credentials. Connect a sender Use Foody-managed connection or the restaurant’s personal Twilio account if offered. A personal sender must already be registered and online with approved Utility templates belonging to the same account. Enter secrets only in the protected form. A failed verification preserves the prior configuration; switching billing modes requires disconnecting first. Use a gated Meta coexistence connection Direct Meta coexistence is a controlled pilot and disabled by default. Connecting alone does not switch message routing; activate the intended provider explicitly after verification. The existing Business app remains available. Do not assume fallback to Twilio if a Meta send fails. Read message history In the order’s communication panel inspect sent, delivered, read, failed and blocked-before-send records. A blocked automation is not proof of delivery. For a reviewed courier reminder use its explicit action only when eligible. Unknown provider outcomes are not automatically replayed; investigate before another send. Create a model with a photo or PDF In Settings → Communications → WhatsApp, a user with settings-edit permission can open Create a model. Choose the notification type, language and a new name, then Message attachment: Photo or PDF document. Upload a JPEG/PNG up to 5 MB for a photo, or a PDF up to 10 MB for a fixed document. For each order’s own receipt, choose PDF document then Document to send → Receipt for this order. The server uses a fictional sample document for Meta approval. Review the text and submit. Wait for Utility approval before assigning the model to a notification. Creation in Foody prepares the approval sample; for a model edited directly in Meta, see image synchronization below. Manage files and check sends Files are available to authorized restaurant users through attachment configuration, without a public storage link. Preview file opens an authenticated preview. Delete file requires confirmation and refuses files referenced by a notification, saved stage or pending message. Replace the file in those settings and save first. The library allows 40 files and 100 MB per restaurant. If upload or deletion is unconfirmed, refresh the list before retrying. If transfer to Meta fails, Foody does not send the text alone or switch to Twilio. In the order → Customer messages, check the attachment filename recorded with the attempt and the status returned by WhatsApp; Read depends on WhatsApp’s return. Review a route-based delivery reminder For an assigned delivery with a saved customer-window setting, reminders use the route arrival plus the configured duration, rather than the order’s broad scheduled slot. For example, arrival at 08:30 and 90 minutes produces 08:30–10:00. Configure it in Orders → Deliveries → allocation, beside the time at each stop, and review the manual or approved WhatsApp preview before sending. The same range supplies Twilio, Meta and stage reminders; existing template variables and J-1 eligibility remain in effect. Unconfigured historic routes keep the original saved slot. If the range cannot be verified, recalculate the route and reopen the reminder. A changed approved preview must be reviewed again before sending. Editing a template alone does not calculate a route or change its margin. Choose how to send a reminder Approved WhatsApp reminders can be previewed early, while manual buttons remain blocked until the day before delivery in the restaurant’s timezone. Orders → Deliveries → WhatsApp reminders reviews and confirms reminders across every route on the selected date; WhatsApp customer and Send this reminder handle one customer. Messages use the saved route’s calculated arrival window and assigned courier. Manual buttons use the global reminder template; automatic stages retain their explicitly configured template and timing in Order workflow. For day-before-only sending, select that timing on the intended stage, for example Ready. Opening a preview enables no trigger. A previously submitted, uncertain or failed reminder is never sent again by another mode, even if its text or provider changes. Changes before sending require a refreshed preview. Acceptance does not prove delivery; consult Customer messages on the order. Preview text represents the current calculation, not an earlier stored message. Send WhatsApp messages for one or several orders Prerequisites: permission to manage orders. Sending from Foody requires an already configured, active business number and approved model. Creating or editing models still requires settings access. 1. In order details, click Send a WhatsApp message beneath the customer’s contact details or in Actions . For several orders, select list rows and click the same button. Selection covers only the displayed page, up to 25 orders; changing filters, date, page or restaurant clears it. 2. Choose WhatsApp Business to send from Foody, or WhatsApp app to prepare editable text and send it yourself. 3. With Business, choose Order confirmation , Delivery reminder or Satisfaction after an order . Foody uses the configured approved global model, including its actual language and attachment. This panel cannot send free text through the API or choose an arbitrary library model. Select each recipient to check the phone, sender and exact content. Click an attachment’s filename to preview it. 4. Only ready previews can be sent. Missing details, reminders that are not due and previous attempts stay visible. Reminders retain their sending-date policy and need the saved delivery window and assigned courier; satisfaction requires a completed delivery or pickup order and active configuration. Click Send message or Send N messages . For multiple selected orders, confirm the eligible count. Each order produces a separate message; one customer with several orders may receive several messages. 5. In the app channel, choose confirmation, delivery information or receipt link. Language starts with the customer’s language, falling back to the restaurant’s language. Each draft and language can be edited. Open WhatsApp opens only the selected conversation; send inside WhatsApp, then return to select the next recipient. Foody reports only WhatsApp opened , without claiming sending or delivery. Discarding edited text requires confirmation. Result and recovery: Business statuses distinguish acceptance from delivery and reading when reported by the provider. Refresh checks the original attempt without resending it. A lost response remains unconfirmed and is never replayed automatically. If an order or model changes, remaining sends stop: refresh and review again. Correct missing saved details or configuration, then refresh unavailable previews. Allow pop-ups if the app does not open. Customer messages retains tracked history. Workflow automations keep their configured models and triggers; opening this panel does not activate or change them. Automatically retrieve the Meta template image Prerequisite: an approved Utility template with a Photo header in the connected Meta account. In Settings → Communications → WhatsApp, open Configure for the message: Foody reloads the templates and automatically retrieves their Meta image. The preview displays the image above the text without uploading a file to Foody. An existing selection without a file also follows the Meta image. If you previously selected a local image, choose Image from Meta template under Photo, then Done and Save to use Meta’s image. Explicit local file selections are preserved. Refresh templates and connection reloads edits made in Meta. Satisfaction and workflow-stage previews also use this image; the order composer displays the actual attachment. The image must be a JPEG/PNG accessible from Meta, up to 5 MB. If retrieval fails, the preview offers Refresh and sending fails without a text-only fallback. Check the image in Meta if its link is unavailable. An image changed after a manual send was prepared requires a new preview before sending. Opening and refreshing never sends a message. Choose the customer WhatsApp recipient If the customer uses a different WhatsApp number, open Clients → their profile, select Use for WhatsApp under Phone numbers and save. That number is used by Meta and Twilio messages and by WhatsApp app handoffs from the order, including link and document sharing. The order phone remains its contact and SMS-verification number. Check the preview recipient; changing the WhatsApp selection requires a new reviewed preview before an API send. Saving the customer profile sends no test message.

articles.title: Customers, addresses and duplicates
articles.description: Admin → Clients
articles.body: Admin → Clients Availability and access Editing and merging require customer-management permission. Find a customer Search the customer list and inspect name, phone, address, order count and last order. Check the intended person before editing. Edit the customer profile Open the profile from the customer phone, edit the name, phone numbers, address and delivery details, then save. Review addresses on existing orders separately. Authorize cash ordering Use the trusted/cash-allowed setting only for the intended customer. This controls cash ordering eligibility, not evidence of an actual payment. Merge duplicates Review selected customer profiles and phone numbers before confirming a merge. Check the resulting combined profile and avoid merging different people. Manage phones and choose the WhatsApp number With customer-management permission, select the customer phone to open Edit customer. Under Phone numbers, correct Primary phone or choose Add a phone number. Enter a complete number; Israeli numbers are saved with +972 without the national trunk zero and foreign numbers retain their country code. Select Use for WhatsApp on the number that should receive messages, even when the calling number differs. Exactly one WhatsApp recipient is selected; a customer can have up to ten numbers. Save confirms profile and phone changes together. Invalid input, duplicate numbers or a number belonging to another record blocks this save and retains the draft; use Merge customers to associate existing records. Removing an additional number takes effect only on Save and separates its history without deleting its orders. Correcting the primary retains names, addresses and grouping and corrects existing order contacts. Login accounts and other restaurants remain unchanged. Cash eligibility belongs to the same customer; adding a number does not create another cash authorization. To correct several customers together, select at least two rows and choose Actions → Correct phones. The batch is atomic; a conflict blocks every correction. After a completed save and failed refresh, Retry reloads without repeating the write. Format validation does not prove ownership or WhatsApp registration.

articles.title: Courier itinerary and delivery completion
articles.description: Admin → Orders → Courier mode, or assigned courier workspace
articles.body: Admin → Orders → Courier mode, or assigned courier workspace Open the assigned itinerary In Foody Admin courier mode, select your route from the list at the top, including future assignments. An active route is selected on opening. The map and numbered pins are visible immediately; on desktop, the timeline sits alongside it. Check the date, addresses, calculated times, contacts and instructions. Finish, distance and duration are plan estimates; an incomplete calculation hides them. The round menu opens account, restaurant, language and theme controls. Use only orders within your authorized courier scope. In the courier view, the order amount is shown only for cash payments. Card payments, other payment methods and orders with an unknown payment method do not show an amount. Navigate and contact Select an address in the timeline or its map pin to select that stop and reveal its actions. A pin scrolls the list without confirming delivery. Fixed Navigate and Mark delivered buttons target the same selected stop, whose number and address appear above under Selected stop. Check this destination before acting. Select the phone number to call or WhatsApp to prepare a message. Unverified addresses remain flagged before a navigation search. Stop options let you correct the address or move the stop up/down; confirm a correction with dispatch. Confirm the actual result After Start, select the delivery actually handed over in the list or on the map, check its number and address under Selected stop, then choose Mark delivered. Without an explicit selection, the next unfinished stop is proposed. After a successful confirmation, the next remaining stop is proposed, but no other order is delivered automatically. Mark arrived remains optional. A finished stop cannot be confirmed again using the fixed button. If the route was cancelled, is no longer active or the order was reassigned to another courier, the server rejects confirmation without completing the order or the other route: refresh or reopen your routes and select the current assignment. A failure displays an error and preserves remaining deliveries. Delivery confirmation does not itself collect an unpaid balance. Edit endpoints and start the route Before departure, open Adjust at the bottom of your assigned route, then Edit. Settings are also available in Route options. After saving, close the panel to return to the map. The menu also offers Re-optimize, which changes the order unlike a simple search. Set departure time, departure address and final destination; use the address suggestions or enter a complete address manually. Set the customer window and handover duration separately, then save and review the recalculated sequence. Changing an endpoint resets manual ordering. Start route confirms that the assigned unfinished deliveries are leaving and changes accepted, preparing and ready deliveries together to Out for delivery. Finished/cancelled deliveries are not reopened. A held kitchen course or an unsettled weight order must be resolved first. If departure fails, no partial status change is saved. A courier can have only one active route; finish it before starting another. Before departure, departure and final addresses remain editable after allocation. Include the house number, street and city; the number may appear before or after the street name, and the displayed address is retained. If Address not found appears, check the number and city, then select another suggestion or correct the full address. A temporary location-service failure requires trying again later. The saved route remains unchanged on either failure. When Google is active in Maps and routes, departure and final addresses can use a precise Google match even when Geoapify cannot locate them. Save the route settings before departure and review the recalculated final leg. If Google is unavailable or its protected quota is exhausted and the other provider cannot locate an endpoint, saving or recalculation is blocked and the previous plan is retained; the final destination is never silently omitted. Google-only points are shown on the Google map and hidden when the map switches provider. Select a precisely located alternative or try again when Google becomes available. Enable Respect order time windows only when saved order times are agreed customer commitments. Disabled by default, this option allows stop optimization before deriving customer arrival ranges. Changing it recalculates even a previous manual sequence; review the result before departure. Respond to a mapping service limit An exhausted-quota or unavailable-service warning does not mean the customer address is wrong. Known Google positions remain on the Google map while their cache is valid; unchecked positions are marked temporarily unavailable. Paths and arrivals that cannot be calculated stay hidden. Ask dispatch to check Usage and quotas and wait for service availability, then refresh and recalculate if needed. Do not remove a delivery to dismiss the warning. Orders and addresses are retained. Review recalculated times before contacting customers. Adjust the map and find a stop On mobile, drag the handle above the list to choose a compact, balanced or expanded view. Keyboard Up/Down and Home/End provide the same adjustment. The list scrolls independently of the fixed actions. Search stops filters by address, city, customer, phone, order number or instructions without changing the route; clear or close search to restore all stops. Selecting a pin clears the filter and reveals its stop. Fit the whole route reframes the map; + and − control zoom. Viewing another route does not stop active-route location sharing when the phone permits it. Correct a test departure If you start a route accidentally, tell a manager before recording any arrival or delivery. In Orders → Deliveries, a user with order-management permission can choose Undo departure while every stop is pending, then unassign and reallocate the route. Out for delivery orders return to In preparation and the replacement courier can start after reassignment. Courier mode does not offer this management correction. Previously sent messages remain in the history. View another courier’s workspace With a superadmin account, open the relevant restaurant, then Orders → Courier mode. Under View as courier, select a courier from that restaurant; the first in the list is selected initially. You see the same map, unfinished routes and stops as that courier. Change the selection at any time to display the new courier’s routes; the previous selected stop, search and panels are reset. Displayed actions, including Start route and Mark delivered, really change that courier’s deliveries: use them only to record work that has taken place. The signed-in account remains superadmin and its GPS position is not reported as the courier’s. Other accounts keep their own routes without this selector. If no couriers are configured, have the restaurant’s team roles checked. If loading fails, choose Retry; a removed membership or a courier from another restaurant is rejected by the server.

articles.title: Dispatch and route planning
articles.description: Admin → Orders → Deliveries / Delivery tours
articles.body: Admin → Orders → Deliveries / Delivery tours Refund or void a Verifone online payment The Admin order payment section supports total or partial matched refunds and total VOID for an eligible single Verifone online payment, for owners/managers with payments.manage. Provider state, captured amount and verified history govern eligibility, not a fixed 24-hour rule. This does not cancel preparation or fulfillment and does not add a POS terminal refund button. Unknown results stay reserved and must be checked, never resubmitted. Invoice4U credit/cancellation documents require a separate check. See the online payment procedure. A captured ABS sale still AUTHORISED/AUTHORIZED or SETTLEMENT REQUESTED is not settled: Admin shows Available to void and only Void entire payment, with no prior refund. Refund payment and Available to refund require an explicit settled state or verified partially-refunded history. Generic APPROVED/COMPLETED, contradictory states or missing evidence offer neither action. A state change before confirmation rejects the stale action; it never switches VOID to REFUND automatically. Request rejected by Verifone means no return of funds is confirmed, not necessarily an issuer decline. Review the by-weight authorization ceiling For online by-weight orders, open Settings → Payments & VAT with settings.edit. Set Weight hold buffer % from 0 to 100 and save; the default for new restaurants is 20. A failed save keeps the draft. Zero still authorizes the estimate. Only the weight-priced subtotal gets a margin: 100 weighted + 50 fixed at 20% authorizes 170; delivery has no extra margin. Checkout shows the estimate, temporary ceiling and Confirm and authorize, in the restaurant theme. A changed ceiling requires customer review and another confirmation before payment; unknown policy blocks authorization. Existing reviewed checkouts and holds keep their ceiling. Staff confirm measured weights before capture and progression; excess beyond the hold is flagged for a separate payment, never automatically charged. Cash/pay-later makes no hold promise. Requires a configured authorize/capture provider, with partial capture, release and expiry validated before production. This neither changes the catering deposit/balance policy nor enables new-card saving with a CST weighted hold. Select deliveries for one date Choose the route date and review available delivery orders. Do not combine scheduled deliveries from another service date into the route. Assign couriers and stops Select the intended courier, depot and orders, then review stop addresses, service times and promised windows. Correct an address before optimization. Review a calculated route Calculate the route or fleet allocation, then review the route before departure. By default, saved order slots do not constrain stop order: they may have been assigned automatically. Enable Respect order time windows only when those times have been agreed with customers. When enabled, couriers can receive different stop counts and planning can serve the earliest deadline first; each complete route must satisfy the enabled windows. Distinguish driving, waiting and handover. A rejected plan can concern departure, enabled windows or road access. Review these settings before retrying; recalculations and unsuccessful attempts can consume provider usage. Choose the route time constraints In Orders → Deliveries, open allocation or Edit on a draft route. Respect order time windows is off by default: the route optimizes stop order, then calculates arrivals and the customer communication range. Enable it only for saved times actually agreed with customers. The choice is saved per route; changing it and saving recalculates stop order even if it was manual. Existing routes keep their sequence until an explicit recalculation: use Recalculate to correct an existing route. Delivery dates remain enforced and saved order slots are not erased. Review the new estimates and reopen reminder previews before sending. An already sent message is not sent again automatically. Save and track progress Save the reviewed route and use the dispatch controls. Monitor courier/order progress and update a changed plan deliberately instead of assuming the original route remains valid. Courier mode uses a map and timeline with a route selector at the top. The courier finds Adjust and Start in the fixed bar, followed by navigation and delivery confirmation for the next stop. Viewing a pin or searching a stop does not change the saved order. In the courier view, the order amount is shown only for cash payments. Card payments, other payment methods and orders with an unknown payment method do not show an amount. In the courier workspace, fixed Navigate and Mark delivered buttons target the stop selected in the list or on the map; its number and address appear above. An old page cannot confirm delivery from a cancelled or inactive route, or after the order was reassigned to another courier. After rejection, refresh the routes and select the current assignment. Set each courier’s departure and final address Before departure, edit the route in Orders → Deliveries, or define each courier’s endpoints during allocation. Type at least three characters in Departure address or Final destination and select a suggestion. A city alone, such as Raanana, uses its center; choose a complete address for a precise point. The selected label is retained without adding the city again. Street-only suggestions still require a house number for a precise address. If suggestions are unavailable, type a city or full address manually. Save, then review the recalculated final leg and arrival times. Changing an endpoint resets manual stop order; saved order windows apply only when Respect order time windows is enabled. A city endpoint does not replace precise customer addresses. An unresolved street is never substituted with the city center. If an address cannot be found, select a city suggestion or correct the street, number and city. Failed lookups preserve the saved route. With Google active in Maps and routes, endpoints can use a Google match even when Geoapify cannot locate them. If Google is unavailable or its protected quota is reached and the other provider cannot locate the endpoint, saving or recalculation is blocked and the previous plan is retained. The final destination is never silently omitted. Google-only points appear on the Google map and are hidden when the map switches provider. Select a located alternative or retry when Google is available. Set the customer delivery range In allocation, use Customer delivery window beside Time at each stop. New plans propose 90 minutes. Enter 1:30, 1h30 or 90 for an hour and a half; the allowed range is 1–720 minutes. The range begins at the calculated arrival, rounded down to its displayed minute: 08:30 plus 90 minutes gives 08:30–10:00. It does not extend the handover time or change the order’s original scheduling constraints. The setting is saved per route and can be edited before departure. Delivery WhatsApp links and manual/approved reminders use this range. Reopen a reminder after recalculation to review its updated text. Historic routes without this setting retain their saved reminder slot. If a configured route cannot provide a valid arrival, recalculate or correct its address before sending; no guessed range is substituted. This range is calculated after optimization and never becomes a constraint on a later recalculation. Only Respect order time windows enables the slots already saved on orders as arrival constraints. Attach a file to a WhatsApp reminder With direct Meta notifications enabled, configure the attachment in Settings → Communications → WhatsApp or on the Order workflow stage: an approved photo/PDF header template, an authorized fixed file or that order’s PDF receipt. This selection changes neither the route nor the configured sending time. Review the file in the manual preview and the attachment filename in Customer messages; a filename does not prove delivery. Make a one-order combo exception For a one-order combo exception, an authorized Admin user opens the combo step and selects Choose another item. The replacement is included without a surcharge and is saved on that order only. Fulfillment, scheduling and delivery rules remain unchanged. Review the selected dish and portion in the order details. Guest and POS combo pickers retain the configured composition; arrange an exception through the internal Admin order editor. See the combo guide for quantities, eligibility and recovery. Keep stock provenance when moving fulfillment Predefined item stocks now have a journal under Items & menus → Stock history and on each product. A rotating carte can prepare initial allowances per series and publish them without restoring already committed units. Previous remaining counts are not carried forward. Order changes and pre-production releases use the original frozen pool; a produced item remains consumed. Ingredient/preparation quantities and recipe costs remain separate. See Availability for initial imports, corrections and history filters. Distinguish a service limit from an unlocated address If a route reports an exhausted quota or an unavailable mapping service, open Settings → Usage and quotas with settings view or edit permission. Google routes, geocoding and tiles have separate counters: the map can still display while road calculation is blocked. Road displays and recalculations also consume allowance; the counter is not simply the number of routes created. Previously known Google positions remain visible on the Google map while their cache is valid. A position that cannot be checked is marked temporarily unavailable; this does not prove the address is wrong. Foody hides unavailable paths and arrival estimates. A new assignment requiring these positions is rejected before changing orders if a complete calculation is impossible. Fallback is available only when every included point is independently located without Google. Do not unassign deliveries to resolve a quota: contact Foody to review the limit or wait for the displayed renewal, then refresh and recalculate if needed. Review arrivals and reminder previews before sending. A quota does not delete orders or their addresses. Access the new controls Settings → Usage and quotas displays this restaurant’s Google/Geoapify allowances and usage with settings view/edit permission. Fallback credits and deliveries submitted for optimization are distinct from request counts. Foody adjusts limits without resetting counters. See limits and renewal. Customer sign-in invitations are configured separately in Website → Order journey → Show the sign-in invitation on arrival; off retains a discreet Sign in link. This does not change courier assignment or delivery rules. Preview and send the selected date’s reminders In Orders → Deliveries, select a date and open WhatsApp reminders to review pending customers across all displayed routes. WhatsApp customer opens only that customer’s reminder. The read-only preview uses the approved reminder template, saved recipient, assigned courier and calculated route arrival window. It can be reviewed early; manual sending remains blocked until the day before delivery in the restaurant’s timezone. Use Send this reminder for one customer, or Send reminders and confirm the number of separate messages for the entire date. No WhatsApp group is created. Previously submitted, in-progress, uncertain and unavailable reminders are excluded. Check blocked customers; a preparation failure does not prevent other eligible customers. A changed route or message stops remaining sends: refresh, review and confirm again. A lost send response remains uncertain and is never retried automatically. Acceptance does not prove delivery; check Customer messages on the order. The current preview does not reconstruct an earlier message body. For automatic sending, open Order workflow and configure the reminder template and Day before timing on the intended stage, for example Ready. Opening previews enables no automation. Automatic, grouped and individual modes share protection against a second reminder for the same order, including after template or provider changes. Use the courier’s saved final destination Staff → employee → Edit contact details stores the courier’s default final destination, with an option to use the current home address. The planning drawer pre-fills it for a new route, and the API also applies it if a client omits an override. An explicit route destination, including an explicitly empty field, takes precedence. Editing the departure address retains the proposed final destination. Existing routes with deliveries retain their saved settings when a profile changes; empty courier placeholders use the latest default when first planned. Route endpoint validation and recalculation rules still apply. No staff profile edit starts or recalculates an existing route. POS code at staff activation Staff activation checks the permissions assigned in this restaurant, including custom roles: orders.manage or payments.manage requires a private POS code. Read-only couriers and kitchen-only roles do not need one. Existing unused invitation links apply the same current rule. Changing a role label, courier address or route destination does not grant POS permissions. See activation and recovery. Prepare a business-owned Google account In FoodyAdmin’s Help and support panel, open Google account and API keys guide or choose “How do I prepare my Google account and API keys for Foody?”. The step-by-step Google guide covers accounts, projects, billing, APIs, restrictions and secure handoff to Foody. The same translations feed search and assistant sources. Never paste a key or secret file into the conversation. The assistant explains preparation; it does not collect credentials or activate individual onboarding. Undo an accidental departure With order-management permission, open Orders → Deliveries, select the route date and choose Undo departure. This action is offered only for an active route whose stops are all pending. Confirm: the route returns to a draft and Out for delivery orders return to In preparation. Orders already corrected to Accepted, In preparation or Ready for delivery keep their status. The courier remains assigned; then use Unassign and allocate the orders to the correct courier. The date, addresses, stop order and payments are preserved. This undo sends no customer message or kitchen ticket; previously sent messages and their history are retained. If an arrival, delivery or skipped stop has been recorded, or the route changed meanwhile, undo is rejected: refresh and review progress before another correction. Do not mark orders delivered to unlock an assignment. View another courier’s workspace A superadmin can open Orders → Courier mode and select a restaurant courier under View as courier. The map and routes belong to that courier; actions record real changes and the superadmin’s GPS is not shared for them. See the courier-mode procedure, including switching couriers and recovering from errors.

articles.title: Create your Google account and prepare API keys for Foody
articles.description: Step-by-step guide to a Google account, Cloud project, billing, address, map and route APIs, restricted keys and handoff to Foody.
articles.body: Prepare a Google Cloud project owned by your business. For the initial phase, ask Foody to arrange manual onboarding before sending technical credentials. Availability and access Before you start: the owner or an authorized manager must retain control of the account, billing and keys. Have access to a business email address, a payment method accepted by Google and permission to incur business charges. Current Foody availability: Settings → Delivery → Maps shows the provider and usage; it has no form for business-owned keys. Foody must confirm individual onboarding. This guide prepares your application; it does not guarantee activation or the end of shared usage. Wait for onboarding confirmation before enabling paid services or creating a secret file. The goal is to associate your business’s requests with its own project, usage tracking and Google billing. You do not need a separate account for each employee or end customer. For multiple branches, agree the scope and projects with Foody. 1. Create or choose the business Google account 1. Open Google account sign-up, or sign in to the existing business account and skip to securing it. 2. For a new account, enter the information Google requests: first name, last name and basic details. 3. Choose a Gmail address or the option to use your existing email address. A Gmail address is not required. 4. If Google emails you a verification code, enter it on the Google screen. Create a unique password and complete the checks shown. 5. Open Account security, then 2-Step Verification , and complete setup. Also add a recovery email and phone you control. Result: the business retains account access. Never send its password or sign-in codes to Foody. Google account help. 2. Create a dedicated Google Cloud project 1. Open Google Cloud Console and accept any terms Google presents. 2. Click the project selector at the top, then New project . 3. Use a recognizable name, such as Foody Example Restaurant . Select your business organization if offered. 4. Click Create , then select the project. 5. Copy its Project ID , such as foody-example-restaurant , and retain the project number. The display name and ID are different. Result: a project dedicated to your Foody usage, separate from other businesses’ projects. Google project creation guide. 3. Link your business billing account Complete this after Foody confirms onboarding. 1. Open Billing in the console. 2. Create a billing account or select your business’s existing account. 3. Check the country, currency, business details and payment method directly with Google. 4. Link the new project to this account and verify that billing is active. Result: usage charged to this project is billed by Google to the linked account. Creating a Google account does not make the APIs free. Pricing and any free thresholds depend on the services and Google’s terms; permanent free use is not guaranteed. Google billing help. 4. Enable only the APIs confirmed by Foody In the correct project, open APIs & Services → Library. Find each confirmed API, open its page and click Enable . Foody requirement Google API to find Expected configuration --- --- --- Address suggestions and details of the selected address Places API (New) Server key for address lookup Convert an address to coordinates Geocoding API Delivery server key Road geometry, distances and driving durations Routes API Delivery server key Google basemap in delivery views Map Tiles API Delivery server key Optimize stops and assign couriers Route Optimization API Server authentication using a service account; an API key alone is insufficient Actual availability depends on your Foody release and configuration. For a new project, use Places API (New) and Routes API ; do not follow older tutorials that routinely request Directions, Distance Matrix or Places Legacy. Google Maps setup, Places setup and Legacy services. 5. Create and restrict server API keys 1. Open APIs & Services → Credentials. 2. Click Create credentials → API key . 3. Name the first key Foody – Server addresses . Under API restrictions , choose Restrict key , then only Places API (New) . 4. Create a second key, Foody – Server delivery , restricted to the delivery APIs confirmed in step 4: Geocoding API , Routes API and Map Tiles API , as applicable. 5. For each key, under Application restrictions , select IP addresses and enter only the fixed outbound IPs supplied by Foody. Save. If Foody has not confirmed outbound IPs, stop before using the key. Do not guess an IP, use the POS/router IP or remove restrictions to make a test work. If the hosting setup requires another method, Foody must validate it. A server key is confidential. It has no accompanying “client secret” to create. Google key restrictions. 6. Create a browser key only if Foody requests it The server flow above needs no public key. If Foody confirms that your release calls Google directly in the browser: 1. Create a different key named Foody – Web . 2. Under application restrictions, select Websites and add the exact domains and allowed referrer patterns supplied by Foody, including your custom domain if applicable. 3. Restrict APIs to those explicitly required for this flow, such as Maps JavaScript API and the confirmed compatible Places version. Never reuse a server key. Do not allow all websites or generic preview domains. If an old release requests Places Legacy for a new project, contact Foody to check compatibility. A browser key may be visible in the page; restrictions are essential. Google Maps security practices. 7. Prepare optimization authentication, if requested Only if Foody confirms Google optimization for your business. Route Optimization uses server-side OAuth, not a customer sign-in secret. 1. In the same project, open IAM & Admin → Service Accounts. 2. Click Create service account , name it foody-delivery and continue. Create a service account. 3. Grant it Route Optimization Editor ( roles/routeoptimization.editor ) on this project. Do not grant the general Owner or Editor roles. Google optimization role. 4. Give Foody the service account email and Project ID, without a private key. First confirm authentication and secure handoff arrangements. 5. Only if Foody requests a JSON file: open the account → Keys → Add key → Create new key → JSON → Create . Keep the downloaded file in protected storage and send it only through the agreed secure channel. If your organization blocks key creation, request an approved method; do not bypass that policy. Service account key management. This JSON contains a private key: never paste it into chat, ordinary email, a repository or a screenshot. 8. Set alerts and quotas before testing 1. Open Billing → Budgets & alerts . Create a project-scoped budget and choose recipients. 2. Set an amount suitable for your business and alerts, for example at 50%, 80% and 100%. 3. Under Google Maps Platform → Quotas , select each API you use and agree suitable available limits with Foody. 4. Review Google reports by project and service, especially after initial tests. A budget alert does not stop spending. Quotas restrict usage units depending on the API; they do not guarantee an exact monetary cap. A low limit can interrupt addresses or routes. Foody limits and offers remain separate. Control Google Maps costs. 9. Hand your setup over to Foody in two stages First, contact Foody without secrets. Use Contact Foody or your usual contact to request onboarding and a secure handoff channel. The contact form and help assistant are not credential upload channels. You can prepare this message: I would like to use my own Google project for my business. Business name and Foody ID: fill in. Google Project ID: fill in. Requested services: addresses / maps / routes / optimization. Billing active: yes or no. Responsible contact: fill in. Please confirm compatibility, restrictions and a secure credential handoff channel. Then, only after the channel and scope are confirmed: provide the server address key, server delivery key, and only if requested the browser key and service account JSON. Identify each key’s purpose, restrictions and applicable branches. Foody must confirm the association with your business before any billable test. Never send a Google password, verification/recovery codes, banking details, temporary tokens or an OAuth sign-in “client secret”. Do not put keys into order instructions, public website settings or help center chat. 10. Verify activation and your project’s usage Creating keys or selecting Google in Foody does not switch billing by itself. Wait for written confirmation from Foody identifying the services and branches actually connected. If individual onboarding is unavailable, keep the setup in preparation. After confirmed activation, agree a small test that may consume Google quota: 1. Test address search with a public address and no customer data. 2. Check a basemap and a short route; test optimization only if included in onboarding. 3. In Google Cloud, verify that requests appear in your project , by API and key where available. Reports may be delayed. 4. Ask Foody to confirm that the same requests no longer use shared credentials and are scoped to your business. Foody counters alone do not prove which project is billed. Expected result: confirmed services use your project with its restrictions, quotas and billing. Review Foody providers and usage. In courier mode, select the route at the top: map and timeline are visible together. Select a pin to reveal its stop; viewing it changes neither order nor status. Route settings are in Adjust and navigation is in the fixed bar. If a provider switch hides a Google point, check the active provider before correcting the address. For a courier-mode test on real orders, do not confirm an arrival or delivery. If Start was used accidentally, a manager can return to Deliveries and choose Undo departure while all stops are pending, then unassign and reallocate. This correction preserves addresses and map settings; it does not change Google keys, quotas or previously sent messages. 11. Understand other Google services and replace a key Sign in with Google: this uses separate identity configuration. Do not create an OAuth client or sign-in secret for this guide. Document reading: Foody may use Google Cloud Vision for delivery-note OCR when configured. Business-specific Vision onboarding is not offered by the Maps screen; do not enable Cloud Vision API or send another key without a specific Foody request and validation. Google Pay is not configured using these mapping keys. Planned replacement: create a new key with the same restrictions, hand it over securely, wait for switch confirmation and test before deleting the old one. Coordinate service account key replacement the same way. Exposed key or suspicious usage: contact Foody immediately and revoke the compromised key in Google Cloud without waiting for a planned replacement; this may interrupt service. Review your project’s requests and spending. If the operation fails Problem Check and next step --- --- Missing project or creation denied Check the signed-in account and request the necessary permissions from your business Google administrator. Billing inactive Check the account linked to the correct project and payment status with Google. Do not send card details to Foody. API denied / 403 Check project, enabled API, IP/domain restrictions and service account role. Ask Foody to check its configuration without removing restrictions. Quota exceeded / 429 Review quotas and reports before changing a limit. A budget alert does not increase quota. Missing addresses or LegacyApiNotActivatedMapError Ask Foody to verify the Places version and compatibility; do not enable every API at random. Keys created but usage still shared Request individual onboarding confirmation. Creating credentials does not switch anything automatically. When requesting help, provide the step, Project ID, time and a redacted error message. If a screenshot is needed, hide keys, codes, payment and customer information. Google labels may vary with language and account; use the console links above to find the screens.

articles.title: Maps providers and usage
articles.description: Admin → Settings → Delivery → Maps
articles.body: Admin → Settings → Delivery → Maps Review the configured map provider Read the active provider and available usage information. Keep provider credentials in the designated secure configuration; never paste them into support chat. When Google is active in Maps and routes, departure and final addresses can use a precise Google match even when Geoapify cannot locate them. Save the route settings before departure and review the recalculated final leg. If Google is unavailable or its protected quota is exhausted and the other provider cannot locate an endpoint, saving or recalculation is blocked and the previous plan is retained; the final destination is never silently omitted. Google-only points are shown on the Google map and hidden when the map switches provider. Select a precisely located alternative or try again when Google becomes available. Respect usage limits Check map, address-search and route/optimization limits before large planning sessions. A commercial offer does not automatically activate an extra quota or bypass a provider cap. Access the new controls Settings → Usage and quotas displays this restaurant’s Google/Geoapify allowances and usage with settings view/edit permission. Fallback credits and deliveries submitted for optimization are distinct from request counts. Foody adjusts limits without resetting counters. See limits and renewal. Prepare your own Google project To prepare your account, billing and address, map and route keys, follow the step-by-step Google guide. Individual onboarding requires confirmation from Foody: this screen has no form for business-owned keys. First contact Foody without secrets to agree the scope and a secure handoff channel.

articles.title: Delivery zones, fees and calendars
articles.description: Admin → Settings → Delivery
articles.body: Admin → Settings → Delivery Create a delivery zone Create or edit a named zone using the map/address controls. Review its area, active state and ordering eligibility before saving. Set fees and minimums Set the offered fee and minimum-order rules for the zone. Test an address and basket on each boundary; the delivery fee is separate from external courier charges. Configure delivery days and windows Set the zone schedule and offered delivery windows. Where final times are pending, keep that pending state and confirm the real window later from order planning.

articles.title: Set up your restaurant with Foody
articles.description: A practical order for reviewing account access, menus, devices and online ordering.
articles.body: Open the corresponding Foody workspace described below. Review the setup with your Foody representative 1. Activate your account and select the right restaurant. Sign in. 2. Review the restaurant profile, opening hours and order/service settings for your actual operation. 3. Create catalogue items, then place them in customer-facing menu groups. Check channels, hours, prices, variants and modifiers. Items and menus. 4. Review staff roles, employee invitations and activated POS devices. Staff access. 5. If you use online ordering, review the website draft, publish it and check the public ordering link. Website publishing. 6. Confirm your payment provider and receipt/printing setup with Foody before taking live orders. Payment status. 7. Test the intended order flow using the agreed test environment, including preparation and handover. Confirm payment results separately from order status. The enabled modules, hardware and payment methods depend on your installation and contract. Ask Foody to confirm the setup rather than assuming every option is available. Do not submit live payments as test transactions. Prepare a business-owned Google account In FoodyAdmin’s Help and support panel, open Google account and API keys guide or choose “How do I prepare my Google account and API keys for Foody?”. The step-by-step Google guide covers accounts, projects, billing, APIs, restrictions and secure handoff to Foody. The same translations feed search and assistant sources. Never paste a key or secret file into the conversation. The assistant explains preparation; it does not collect credentials or activate individual onboarding.

articles.title: Sign in and recover access
articles.description: Access the Admin and the POS with your own restaurant account.
articles.body: Admin sign-in and account menu Activate an invitation Open the invitation received by email, check the restaurant, choose your password and confirm your contact details. A POS code is requested only when the assigned restaurant permissions allow taking orders (orders.manage) or managing payments (payments.manage). A courier with the usual read-only delivery role, or a kitchen-only role, finishes without this step. A role name alone does not determine the requirement. Never share a password or POS code. Select the restaurant Sign in with your own account, then choose an authorized restaurant. Check its name before editing or exporting data. Recover access After a rejected POS code or failed save, reopen the same still-valid email link and retry; failed activation does not consume it. A duplicate code message means a POS operator must choose a different 4–6 digit code. A courier without POS permissions does not need to try more combinations. If the link is expired, lacks restaurant context or says it was already used and activation did not finish, ask a staff manager to open Staff → Employees → the member → Resend setup invitation. Use the newest email; resending invalidates previous unused links without recreating the member. If activation already succeeded, sign in with the password you chose, or use password recovery. Removed restaurant access must be reviewed by the manager. Never share activation links or credentials with the assistant. Clock in on the terminal On an already enrolled POS, Sign in shows Enter your passcode. Enter your complete personal 4–6-digit code, then tap Start shift. The four slots shown initially expand when you enter a fifth digit; they do not limit an existing code to four digits. Backspace removes the last digit. Entry is not submitted automatically: wait for the sign-in result before using the POS. A rejection displays an error and clears the entry for another attempt; never share your code. Set up this terminal with email and password returns to the sign-in form. A successful PIN session also clocks you in; your account’s role and permissions still apply. Show hours opens a separate flow: checking your status starts neither a shift nor a sales session. See personal time tracking. End a POS shift safely On an enrolled POS, use Sign out in the navigation or End shift in More. If this POS has an open drawer or a pending cash operation, Cash drawer report pending appears before ending the shift. Cancel leaves you signed in; Finish report opens Cash drawer balance without closing anything or signing out. Resolve the pending operation, physically count and close the drawer on the same POS, then request sign-out again and confirm End shift. Without report permissions, ask an authorized manager. An unverifiable cash status keeps the session open; check the connection and retry. A Verifone deposit is separate and never starts automatically. Ending the staff shift keeps this POS enrolled for the next PIN sign-in. See the pending-report procedure. If the End shift response is uncertain, verify it through Retry. Do not recreate a shift end or clear data to bypass an unconfirmed state.

articles.title: How it all connects: from ingredients to a sold-out dish
articles.description: The big picture — how stock, preparations, recipes, items, availability, food cost and orders fit together, and the order to set them up.
articles.body: Open the corresponding Foody workspace described below. The big picture Six pieces work together. Once you understand the chain, everything else clicks: - Stock — the raw ingredients you buy (tomatoes, tuna, oil, buns). - Preparations — things you make from stock in batches (a sauce, a dough, a marinade). - Recipe — what one dish uses: its ingredients and preparations, with quantities. - Item (article) — a dish on your menu, shown to customers inside a menu group. - Availability — computed from the recipe + current stock: low stock or sold-out, automatically. - Food cost — also computed from the recipe. The flow: Stock ┐ ├─→ Recipe ─→ Item ─→ shown to customers Preps ┘ │ ├─→ Availability (low / sold-out, automatic) └─→ Food cost (margin per dish) An order is placed ─→ the recipe is deducted from Stock ─→ Availability updates So a dish isn't an island: it points at a recipe, the recipe points at stock and preparations, and that single link makes availability and food cost work on their own. Set it up in this order Set it up in this order 1. Add your ingredients to Stock Enter the raw ingredients you buy, with their unit and current quantity. → Stock management 2. (Optional) Build your Preparations If you make sauces, doughs or bases in batches, define them once and reuse them across dishes. Producing a batch credits stock; dishes that use it recover automatically. → Preparations 3. Create your items Add each dish to your catalogue (name, price, photo, category). → Creating a menu item 4. Give each item a recipe On the item's Recipe and cost section, link the ingredients and preparations one portion uses, with quantities. This is the link that powers everything downstream. A dish with no recipe is not enough to compute ingredient consumption; check manual availability overrides separately. → Ingredients & portions 5. Put items in a menu group Items only appear to customers once they're in a menu group. → Categories & items 6. Availability now works on its own With recipes in place, dishes go low stock and sold out automatically as stock runs down, and come back when you restock. Tune it with rules, or override a single dish. → Availability What you get once the chain is connected - Automatic sold-out — no more manually switching dishes off when an ingredient runs out. - Accurate food cost — margin per dish, rolled up from the recipe. - Self-updating stock — every order deducts its recipe, so your numbers stay honest. - One place to change things — update a preparation's recipe once and every dish follows. Where to go next - Take and manage orders → Managing orders - Get paid → How payments work - First-time setup checklist → Complete setup guide Prepare a business-owned Google account In FoodyAdmin’s Help and support panel, open Google account and API keys guide or choose “How do I prepare my Google account and API keys for Foody?”. The step-by-step Google guide covers accounts, projects, billing, APIs, restrictions and secure handoff to Foody. The same translations feed search and assistant sources. Never paste a key or secret file into the conversation. The assistant explains preparation; it does not collect credentials or activate individual onboarding.

articles.title: Offers, demo and contacting Foody
articles.description: Visit foody-pos.co.il, choose French, Hebrew or English, then Products, Pricing, Demo or Contact.
articles.body: Visit foody-pos.co.il, choose French, Hebrew or English, then Products, Pricing, Demo or Contact. Compare public offers Review the published POS, Orders, Restaurant, Kitchen and combined offers and their inclusions. Companion belongs to Kitchen. Device licenses cover devices, not a separate charge per employee. Check the current approved pricing page and scoped quote for hardware, external processing, SMS and integrations. Request a demo or support Use Demo/Contact with the requested business contact details and wait for the success confirmation. The Help center is public at /fr/help, /he/help and /en/help. Its assistant answers published procedures and cannot access or change a restaurant account. Do not send secrets or card data.

articles.title: Search and navigate FoodyAdmin
articles.description: Use the search entry in the Admin navigation for the currently selected restaurant.
articles.body: Use the search entry in the Admin navigation for the currently selected restaurant. Find a business record Open search, enter a sufficiently specific term and review grouped item, order, customer and stock results. Use arrows and Enter to open, or Escape to close. Results respect the current restaurant and permissions; an empty result is not proof the record never existed. Filter and inspect a list Use the page’s search, filters, date range, column chooser and pagination where available. Open the row/action menu for its permitted operations. Check active filters before treating a missing record as deleted. Transactions is a separate Admin sidebar destination for confirmed payments; the global search groups items, orders, customers and stock, but is not a payment-history search. Find the item-stock overview Predefined item stocks now have a journal under Items & menus → Stock history and on each product. A rotating carte can prepare initial allowances per series and publish them without restoring already committed units. Previous remaining counts are not carried forward. Order changes and pre-production releases use the original frozen pool; a produced item remains consumed. Ingredient/preparation quantities and recipe costs remain separate. See Availability for initial imports, corrections and history filters.

articles.title: Using Foody help and the assistant
articles.description: Find a guide, ask a question and contact support from FoodyAdmin.
articles.body: Open the corresponding Foody workspace described below. Ask about POS methods without customer data Ask how whole-check methods differ from item preparation options, or where to enable optional customer information. The assistant should cite POS behavior and Order types. It cannot inspect checks, change settings or confirm payment. Use fictional examples, never real customer contacts, card data or terminal identifiers. Find a guide Select Help and support at the bottom of the FoodyAdmin navigation. Open help center opens the guides in a new tab. The public help center also works without signing in. Search a question or browse topics, including items and menus, orders, kitchen, payments, hardware, staff and settings. Search includes article text. Select English, French or Hebrew in the header. Articles awaiting translation remain available in English. Ask a question 1. Open the assistant. 2. Write a question or select a suggestion. 3. Read the answer and open its Sources to check the procedure. 4. Ask a follow-up question. New conversation clears the panel. The assistant explains documented Foody features. It cannot view your account or orders and cannot perform actions. In Admin, the current topic helps find relevant articles; restaurant records and sign-in credentials are not forwarded. Answers can contain errors. Do not share passwords, payment details or personal customer information. Questions and recent conversation turns are sent to our AI provider. The conversation stays in the browser tab's memory; reloading clears it. For receipt or confirmation link previews, ask a general question about the restaurant name or logo and open the cited guide. The assistant uses the published procedure; it cannot open your private link or inspect the order. Do not paste receipt or tracking links into the conversation. For example, ask how to add an item outside the active menus to a staff order. Check the Article library steps in the order guide; the assistant cannot inspect your restaurant’s items or add them to an order. Ask where to find payment history The assistant can point you to the published Transactions procedure for confirmed POS and online payments. It cannot see your restaurant's transactions, inspect a card, confirm an uncertain charge or initiate a refund. Open the actual Transactions screen with the required permission, or ask an authorized operator to reconcile a missing payment before retrying. Contact support Select Contact support to write to support@foody-pos.co.il. Include the product, steps and error message, with sensitive information removed. Sending the email remains an action in your email application. If the assistant is unavailable or its question limit is reached, guides and the support contact remain accessible. Report a procedure that differs from your screen The assistant cannot see your screen or account. If a named button or section no longer exists, give the product, language and guide title, then contact support to correct the procedure. Do not share credentials or customer/payment data. An existing citation alone does not guarantee that every step matches the latest interface. Panel placement can change with language and screen width. Locate a control by its label and documented section rather than an assumed side. In the item editor, the visible side-card headings are Status, Categories and Menus. A suggestion or draft is not a send: purchase generation and supplier transmission are separate actions requiring manual confirmation. Follow the labels displayed in your language: Items & menus → Item library. A question may call this Menu → Items; use the displayed path when following the answer and report a different label. Find delivery planning guidance The delivery guides cover departure/final address suggestions, route order towards the final destination, starting all assigned deliveries together and the customer reminder range. Search for delivery customer window or open Delivery → Dispatch and route planning. Check the installed release before following newly added controls.
