The assistant cites the same published guides; it cannot inspect a courier’s route, change an order or send WhatsApp messages. Find WhatsApp attachment guidance Read Communications → WhatsApp and Message templates to configure a photo, fixed PDF or order PDF receipt with Meta. The guides and assistant use the same published procedure. The assistant explains documented controls; it cannot open private files, inspect orders or confirm message delivery. Check those details in Foody. Photo templates edited directly in Meta can automatically retrieve their image in the Foody preview; see the dedicated section for refresh and retrieval errors. Make a one-order combo exception Ask “How can I replace beef with fish in an internal combo without a surcharge?” The assistant should cite the combo or order guide, explain Choose another item and required orders.manage access, and distinguish the one-order exception from editing the saved definition. It cannot inspect or edit your actual order. Find the mobile address procedure For trouble entering or choosing an address on a phone, search for address or delivery in Help and open Order online as a customer. The assistant cites the same guide in an available language. Check its source and the site release; if the procedure is missing or differs from your screen, contact the restaurant without sharing customer details or payment data with the assistant. On mobile, Pickup and Delivery tabs, the field and the Sign in link at the top keep their positions when the keyboard opens or closes. Compact suggestions show the address and city on two lines in a larger scrolling list. During search, confirmation leaves room for suggestions; it appears after choosing a complete address. The cover is reserved for larger screens. Google Maps attribution and errors stay visible. For a street suggestion without a house number, follow the guide to add the number and choose the complete address; a street alone does not confirm delivery. Find stock movement history To investigate a quantity change, read Availability. Items & menus → Stock history displays movements only, with item, series-date and movement-type filters. Quantities are prepared from the carte. The assistant explains this public procedure without reading your stock or orders. Help with quotas and optional sign-in Help documents restaurant Google/Geoapify usage, monthly limits and renewal under Usage and quotas. It also explains the published sign-in invitation setting and Order without an account. The assistant uses the same public guides: it can explain procedures but cannot read your counters, change allowances or publish your site. For customer sign-in, ask how hiding the invitation differs from disabling an account: direct ordering retains a discreet Sign in link. Support explains the published setting without modifying your site. Prepare a business-owned Google account In FoodyAdmin’s Help and support panel, open Google account and API keys guide or choose “How do I prepare my Google account and API keys for Foody?”. The step-by-step Google guide covers accounts, projects, billing, APIs, restrictions and secure handoff to Foody. The same translations feed search and assistant sources. Never paste a key or secret file into the conversation. The assistant explains preparation; it does not collect credentials or activate individual onboarding. Ask about conditional choices Ask how to configure two-character Number Cake options. The assistant must cite Variants and sizes: one priced format and separate descriptive variant dimensions for the characters, without a surcharge. Modifiers remain actual additions or removals. The assistant uses the published corpus; it cannot inspect your catalog or configure the rules. Ask about sending a WhatsApp message Ask how to send a WhatsApp model for one order or a selection, then check the sources in the WhatsApp guide. The assistant explains the documented Business/app composer, previews and statuses. It cannot read your orders, know whether your customer received a message, change automations or send a message. Check Customer messages on the actual order for recorded evidence; do not paste customer numbers, private links or credentials into the conversation. Check a weekly batch rollover To understand why Home or Orders shows a new empty batch, open Preorders, slots and batches. The batch advances using the restaurant calendar even without an order. The assistant can explain the documented rule and cite its source; it cannot inspect your restaurant settings or orders. Find units and per-size stock guidance Ask how to configure 2,000 g shared across sizes or 1,000 g reserved for each size. Open the cited availability guide to compare tracking modes, portion equivalents, Apply confirmation and conversion of a series with committed orders and recovery after errors. The assistant explains the published procedure; it cannot inspect your quantities or change stock. Check quantities and the series in your management workspace without copying customer data into the question.

articles.title: Submit a catering request
articles.description: Open the restaurant’s Catering service or a delivery-tour/preorder link.
articles.body: Open the restaurant’s Catering service or a delivery-tour/preorder link. Complete a catering flow Select the active service/offer and complete guest count, date/time, choices and contact details. Review the calculated total and whether approval or deposit is required. Submit once and retain the private quote link. A quote awaiting approval is not final acceptance. Order for a specific tour Check the tour’s fulfillment date, ordering window and cutoff before building the basket. A closed/unavailable tour cannot be bypassed with a stale page. Confirm the displayed route/fulfillment information before payment. Enter a valid contact phone Before submitting an order or catering request, enter a complete phone number. In checkout Contact and payment, the initial calling code follows the restaurant country: +33 for France, +972 for Israel, and so on. Choose another calling code for a foreign number, or paste an international number starting with +. Catering assumes Israel for local numbers; foreign numbers need + and their country code. Spaces, dashes and parentheses are accepted; the saved value is international, for example +972502345678. Incomplete numbers, invalid prefixes, letters and extensions block submission and require correction. Phone remains optional for table orders where the form permits it; a supplied number must be valid. Format validation does not check WhatsApp registration. Any SMS verification code still follows the restaurant setting.

articles.title: Order online as a customer
articles.description: Open the restaurant’s public link or select a branch from its chain page.
articles.body: Open the restaurant’s public link or select a branch from its chain page. Review the by-weight authorization ceiling For online by-weight orders, open Settings → Payments & VAT with settings.edit. Set Weight hold buffer % from 0 to 100 and save; the default for new restaurants is 20. A failed save keeps the draft. Zero still authorizes the estimate. Only the weight-priced subtotal gets a margin: 100 weighted + 50 fixed at 20% authorizes 170; delivery has no extra margin. Checkout shows the estimate, temporary ceiling and Confirm and authorize, in the restaurant theme. A changed ceiling requires customer review and another confirmation before payment; unknown policy blocks authorization. Existing reviewed checkouts and holds keep their ceiling. Staff confirm measured weights before capture and progression; excess beyond the hold is flagged for a separate payment, never automatically charged. Cash/pay-later makes no hold promise. Requires a configured authorize/capture provider, with partial capture, release and expiry validated before production. This neither changes the catering deposit/balance policy nor enables new-card saving with a CST weighted hold. Choose a menu, then a group If the restaurant offers several menus on the page, select their tab, such as BASSARI or HALAVI. Only the selected menu’s groups and items appear. Pills or links underneath navigate to its groups, such as Sandwiches or Drinks. Search and the availability filter apply to this menu. A search with no results keeps menu tabs visible; switching menus clears the search. Browsing another menu keeps the basket. If an item is missing, try another menu or clear the search; visibility also depends on availability and publication. For a combo, open its sheet and choose Build your combo: the menu keeps its theme while selecting items. Use the counter and − button to review or remove a pick, then complete the steps before adding to the cart. See website combos. Build a basket Choose pickup, delivery or table ordering when offered, select the active menu and open an item. Choose a variant, required modifiers, quantity and allowed notes, then add it. Review and edit the basket before checkout. A customer assistant suggestion still needs the same required choices and availability checks. Choose an address on a phone In the ordering dialog, choose Delivery and enter the street, house number and city. If address search is enabled, scroll the suggestions and tap the complete address. Selecting a street still requires its house number and keeps the keyboard open. A complete address dismisses the keyboard; review any offered times and tap Confirm address. The button stays disabled while checks run or delivery is unavailable. For pickup, choose Pickup then Confirm pickup. The cross at the top closes the dialog. Account access remains optional. If no address matches, refine the number or city; if the service fails, retry or contact the restaurant. On mobile, Pickup and Delivery tabs, the field and the Sign in link at the top keep their positions when the keyboard opens or closes. Compact suggestions show the address and city on two lines in a larger scrolling list. During search, confirmation leaves room for suggestions; it appears after choosing a complete address. The cover is reserved for larger screens. Google Maps attribution and errors stay visible. After choosing a street, add the house number in the same field and choose the complete address suggestion. A street alone cannot confirm delivery. Choose contact and fulfillment Enter the requested contact details, address or pickup time. For delivery check zone, fee and offered slot; for preorder/tour links follow their specific deadline/date. The final checkout revalidates current rules and prices. Pay and verify confirmation Choose an offered payment method, review total and follow the secure payment flow. Wait for the verified order result. A rejected/pending payment is not a confirmed paid order; keep its reference and ask restaurant support before paying twice. Sign in before ordering Under Sign in, use Google or your email and password. Facebook and Apple appear only when configured. Standalone code sign-in is removed; address-verification and password-recovery codes remain separate. Older accounts without a password can use Forgot password to set one. Checkout offers the same configured providers alongside email/password; only the payment action submits inline enrollment. Guest access remains available, and card saving still needs separate consent. Access the new controls The entry sign-in invitation is controlled in Website → Order journey → Show the sign-in invitation on arrival. Off goes directly to pickup/delivery details; when on, Order without an account remains immediately visible. Save the draft and publish to apply this choice. See the journey setting. When the invitation is off, a discreet Sign in link remains available in the pickup or delivery dialog. It opens authentication only when selected; dismissing authentication retains entered details and allows ordering without an account. Check conditional item choices An item configured with repeated positions requires one separate choice per position according to the selected format. For example, a two-character Number Cake accepts 11, AB or A7. The format price replaces the base price; modifiers add only their configured surcharges. Reducing the position count removes newly hidden choices. Positions remain distinct in the cart, orders and kitchen ticket; review them before confirming. These customizations do not change delivery, availability, recipe, discount or cancellation rules. Configuration requires compatible versions and menu editing permission. See Variants and sizes for setup and recovery after a rejected selection. Enter a valid contact phone Before submitting an order or catering request, enter a complete phone number. In checkout Contact and payment, the initial calling code follows the restaurant country: +33 for France, +972 for Israel, and so on. Choose another calling code for a foreign number, or paste an international number starting with +. Catering assumes Israel for local numbers; foreign numbers need + and their country code. Spaces, dashes and parentheses are accepted; the saved value is international, for example +972502345678. Incomplete numbers, invalid prefixes, letters and extensions block submission and require correction. Phone remains optional for table orders where the form permits it; a supplied number must be valid. Format validation does not check WhatsApp registration. Any SMS verification code still follows the restaurant setting. Control weekly ordering manually When a restaurant manages weekly ordering manually, its team opens and pauses orders without an automatic reopening time. You can still browse the menu during a pause. When ordering is open, choose one of the offered delivery/collection dates; manual opening does not remove product preparation, stock, payment or delivery requirements. Orders already confirmed retain their saved date and status. If ordering is paused, wait for the restaurant to reopen it rather than relying on a displayed weekly opening time. Product photos An item can show several photos. See Product photos for adding photos, selecting the cover and using the dots, arrows or horizontal swipe in product details. A single photo has no gallery controls.

articles.title: Order from a table QR
articles.description: Scan the restaurant’s table QR and verify the displayed table before ordering.
articles.body: Scan the restaurant’s table QR and verify the displayed table before ordering. Join the correct table Open the signed QR link and follow the available session/guest flow. An expired or invalid link must be renewed by staff. Do not change table IDs or reuse another table’s link to bypass access. Order and request assistance Select items and required choices, review the basket and use the payment/ordering options enabled for this table. Use assistance controls when offered. Staff bill splitting and guest QR payments can have different capabilities; do not assume every POS action is available on the guest page. When staff close the table A confirmed staff closure ends the table session and its active assistance requests together. A failed closure leaves the existing table and session unchanged; the closure notification is not sent before confirmation. If service changes while an order is being submitted, that order cannot be attached to the expired or replacement session. Ask staff to verify or reopen the table, then refresh before reviewing the basket again. Do not repeat a payment or reuse an old session link to force an order through.

articles.title: Track orders, receipts and saved methods
articles.description: Use the confirmation/tracking link or the restaurant’s order-history/account entry.
articles.body: Use the confirmation/tracking link or the restaurant’s order-history/account entry. Sign in before ordering At the start of the Pickup/Delivery dialog, choose Sign in or Continue as a guest below it. Both are text actions, without a filled sign-in button. No address field or confirmation button appears before this choice. Sign-in offers Google or email verification; closing it returns to the choices. The benefit text covers saved address/payment methods/orders for Delivery and saved details/payment methods/orders for Pickup. Continue as a guest reveals address entry for Delivery; Pickup shows collection details and menu access without asking for a delivery address. Back returns to the choices without clearing the draft. The guest choice is retained when switching services and closing/reopening this dialog. Signed-in customers proceed directly: a saved address with a validated selection offers Use this address and Edit. Incomplete addresses still require completion. Signing in after starting an address retains the draft. Saving a payment method remains a separate checkout choice. Sign in opens Google and the email/password form. Facebook and Apple appear only when configured by the service. Standalone email-code sign-in is no longer offered. Account creation, address verification and password-recovery codes remain separate. Read the current order state Open tracking and review the latest saved status and fulfillment information. Contact the restaurant for an operational change; the Foody help assistant cannot edit the order. Keep private tracking/receipt links out of public messages. Access history and receipts Complete the offered customer authentication/verification, then open the correct restaurant’s history. Select an order to view its digital receipt and available print/share/new-order actions. Reopening a receipt does not create a new order or payment. Manage payment enrollment If offered, explicitly opt into saving a payment method and complete the provider’s flow. Review the account’s saved-method state afterwards. Remove the Foody authorization through the account controls when needed; this does not cancel unrelated subscriptions with the provider. Check receipt and confirmation link previews Check that the restaurant has a name and logo configured, then share a valid receipt or order-confirmation link with its intended recipient. The link preview uses that restaurant’s name and logo, independently of the website’s general share image. Without a logo, the preview shows a card with the restaurant’s name. It does not include customer details, order lines or amounts. The linked page can still contain private order information: do not publish the link publicly. If the wrong identity appears, check that the link belongs to the intended restaurant and that its configured logo is accessible. An expired or invalid receipt cannot provide a restaurant preview. Choose a sign-in method Choose Google, Facebook or Apple when its button is offered, then complete authorization in the provider window. Cancellation does not replace the order draft. For email, enter your address and password under Sign in. If an older email-code account has no password, use Forgot password to set one after proving ownership; orders remain on that account. Creating an account may require address verification, and recovery still uses its separate code. Apple Hide My Email is supported. Switching providers does not guarantee account merging: if history is missing, use the original method and correct restaurant. A Facebook contact email never grants another account’s history. If a provider is absent or fails, use Google, password or guest access. Signing in does not consent to card storage. Understand sign-in data Configured providers may load their library when their choices are displayed and process browser/network information under their policy. Sign-in supplies Foody with a provider identifier and the supplied name, email or photo, not your Google, Apple or Facebook password. Apple may hide the email address. Foody keeps the session in an HttpOnly cookie and temporary authentication state; provider tokens are not persisted in Web Storage or these authentication logs. You can continue as a guest. To request account deletion, use the contact in Foody’s privacy policy; deletion is not a refund action. Sign in while ordering When the invitation is off, a discreet Sign in link remains available in the pickup or delivery dialog. It opens authentication only when selected; dismissing authentication retains entered details and allows ordering without an account. Correct a saved phone number A saved or previously verified number restores its own calling code, even when its country differs from the restaurant. An empty field defaults to the restaurant country. At checkout, a saved phone must pass the same validation as a new number. If it is invalid, contact details stay open for correction. Choose the correct country code or enter the international number with +, then review the order before confirming. The saved format is international and compatible with WhatsApp messaging. This does not prove ownership or WhatsApp registration and does not change your sign-in method. To save the corrected contact details in your account, use the remember-details preference offered at checkout.

articles.title: Availability (sold-out & low stock)
articles.description: Configure item stock, its availability rule and manual status in the current item editor.
articles.body: Items & menus → Item library → saved item → Stock & availability. Open Stock & availability For items still using persistent legacy stock, open a saved item from Items & menus → Item library and scroll to Stock & availability. The table shows the item, quantity and status. Editing requires menu editing permission. This section is part of the continuous editor, not a panel under a Recipe tab. Choose the stock basis With menu editing permission, open a saved product → Stock & availability → Edit stock and availability. The Availability badge in Items or a Carte opens the same editor for current stock. Opening it changes nothing. Choose Available without limit, Unavailable, Manually defined quantity or Quantity calculated from recipe. Manual quantity is the remaining stock entered in units, g/ml or per size; existing commitments remain reserved. Recipe calculation uses available ingredients and preparations and stops applying the manual counter. Old counters and frozen reservations remain intact for existing orders. Without recipe ingredients, no quantity limit can be calculated: a message asks you to complete the recipe. If ready-stock sale is active, disable it in the preparation settings and save the product before choosing recipe calculation. Choose and manage a rule Advanced stock settings start collapsed. Open them to choose the Stock profile. Use the default setting inherits the category profile, then the restaurant profile; a named profile such as Standard is an explicit choice. The profile controls stock tracking, the low-stock threshold, displaying the remaining count and hiding the product or marking it sold out when empty. A summary describes the selected profile. If the profile does not track stock, a visible message says sales are not limited by stock. Available without limit and Unavailable keep priority. The profile belongs to the product across all series; quantities and the stock source apply to the displayed series, or the product stock outside series. Override status and save Apply directly saves every setting in this dialog: availability, source, tracking mode, unit, quantities and profile. This works with or without series, without product Save. Unsaved names, prices and preparation settings stay independent and are not saved. A profile-only change does not rewrite stock or reservations, including exhausted stock and inactive products. Stock and profile changes submitted together commit in one transaction: failure rolls back both and retains inputs. Dialog controls are locked while saving. Cancel or Escape before applying discards choices; after confirmation, leaving the product does not undo the applied settings. If saving succeeds but refreshing fails, Retry only reloads data without repeating the adjustment. Edit reusable profiles in Settings → Stock → Availability. Check calculation and size quantities For items still using persistent legacy stock, actions → View availability calculation opens capacity details: possible sales, calculation basis and limiting ingredient when present. When tracking sizes separately, check each quantity. Item stock differs from recipe consumption quantities and the Active/Inactive filter in the Items library. An unavailable calculation is an error to investigate, not zero stock. Verify after saving After Apply, reopen the dialog and verify quantity, profile and availability, then the relevant web or POS channel. Visibility also depends on groups, channels and schedules. Retry failed loading before applying. Unsaved name and preparation changes retain the product Save action. Items and menus · Recipe and quantities · Stock. Prepare stock for a new series With menu editing permission, open the rotating carte, select a series and open the “…” menu beside the title → Prepare stocks for this series. Enter INITIAL allowances including quantities already ordered: available = initial minus committed. Use shared units, compatible base measures (g/ml), counts per size, or no predefined limit. Copy previous initial quantities copies allowances, never previous remaining quantities or an old sold-out override. Quantities are shared by the same restaurant item across cartes for that series. Save draft keeps preparation private; Publish applies it atomically without restoring reservations made while editing. The first activation imports current available stock and existing scheduled orders, preserving current remaining quantities. Later series never inherit the old global counter. No predefined limit may still be constrained by a recipe, rule or manual status. Investigate stock changes Open Items & menus → Stock history. This page contains only the movement journal, visible as soon as it opens: it does not list current stock or offer corrections. Choose an Item or All Items, a Series date or All series, and a Movement or All movements. Past series dates are accepted. Filters combine and remain applied when using Show more. The journal shows the date and series, item, movement, before/after quantities and actor; a link opens the associated order when present. An empty result means no movements were recorded for those filters. Initial imports are labeled as imports; changes before tracking was activated cannot be reconstructed. If the item filter fails, Retry reloads that filter while the journal remains available. On a product, the Stock history button opens a dedicated dialog containing only that item’s movements, across all series. On a carte, the row History shortcut or its “…” menu also opens that dialog. To prepare or adjust initial series quantities, open the carte, choose the series, then Prepare stocks for this series, save the draft and publish after reviewing it. Availability actions marked immediate remain separate and journaled. A pre-production cancellation credits the original pool; a produced item remains consumed. If the journal fails to load, Retry reloads movements without changing filters; this error is not presented as an empty history. Manage a product tracked by series With menu editing permission, open a saved product → Stock & availability → Edit stock and availability. The Availability badge in Items or a Carte opens the same editor for current stock. Opening it changes nothing. Choose Available without limit, Unavailable, Manually defined quantity or Quantity calculated from recipe. Manual quantity is the remaining stock entered in units, g/ml or per size; existing commitments remain reserved. Recipe calculation uses available ingredients and preparations and stops applying the manual counter. Old counters and frozen reservations remain intact for existing orders. Without recipe ingredients, no quantity limit can be calculated: a message asks you to complete the recipe. If ready-stock sale is active, disable it in the preparation settings and save the product before choosing recipe calculation. Apply directly saves every setting in this dialog: availability, source, tracking mode, unit, quantities and profile. This works with or without series, without product Save. Unsaved names, prices and preparation settings stay independent and are not saved. A profile-only change does not rewrite stock or reservations, including exhausted stock and inactive products. Stock and profile changes submitted together commit in one transaction: failure rolls back both and retains inputs. Dialog controls are locked while saving. Cancel or Escape before applying discards choices; after confirmation, leaving the product does not undo the applied settings. If saving succeeds but refreshing fails, Retry only reloads data without repeating the adjustment. Edit reusable profiles in Settings → Stock → Availability. Change availability from Items With menu editing permission, open a saved product → Stock & availability → Edit stock and availability. The Availability badge in Items or a Carte opens the same editor for current stock. Opening it changes nothing. Choose Available without limit, Unavailable, Manually defined quantity or Quantity calculated from recipe. Manual quantity is the remaining stock entered in units, g/ml or per size; existing commitments remain reserved. Recipe calculation uses available ingredients and preparations and stops applying the manual counter. Old counters and frozen reservations remain intact for existing orders. Without recipe ingredients, no quantity limit can be calculated: a message asks you to complete the recipe. If ready-stock sale is active, disable it in the preparation settings and save the product before choosing recipe calculation. Apply directly saves every setting in this dialog: availability, source, tracking mode, unit, quantities and profile. This works with or without series, without product Save. Unsaved names, prices and preparation settings stay independent and are not saved. A profile-only change does not rewrite stock or reservations, including exhausted stock and inactive products. Stock and profile changes submitted together commit in one transaction: failure rolls back both and retains inputs. Dialog controls are locked while saving. Cancel or Escape before applying discards choices; after confirmation, leaving the product does not undo the applied settings. If saving succeeds but refreshing fails, Retry only reloads data without repeating the adjustment. Edit reusable profiles in Settings → Stock → Availability. Within a carte draft, applied stock replaces only this item’s stock preparation; other drafts stay private. Stock loads freshly on opening. On conflict, reload, review quantities and explicitly apply again. Identify the variant to prepare For an item with position choices, check the characters and their order on the order and ticket. Kitchen counters distinguish choice combinations so two products with the same format are not confused. Availability and stock movements continue to use the item and its priced format; a descriptive character creates no surcharge or second stock debit. Choose units and shared or per-size stock With menu editing permission, open a series-tracked product → Stock & availability → Edit stock and availability, or the Availability badge in Items or a Carte. Select Manually defined quantity. Choose the tracking mode, including for a series that already has committed orders: Shared unit count deducts one per item; Shared measure pools a budget across sizes; Count per size keeps an independent counter for each variant. Compatible numeric sizes offer g/kg or ml/l under Input unit. For example, 2,000 g in shared measure is shared between the 250 g and 500 g sizes. In count per size, entering 1,000 g for each allows 4 portions of 250 g and 2 portions of 500 g, with no sharing between counters. Check the displayed equivalents: each per-size budget must equal a whole number of portions. A blank size remains unlimited; enter 0 to exhaust it, with at least one other positive size. Use Unavailable to exhaust the whole item. Changing g to kg or ml to l preserves the quantity; changing tracking mode clears the fields to avoid converting portions into grams. When the mode changes, existing reservations are recalculated from each ordered size and added to the remaining quantity you enter: 2 portions of 250 g and 1 of 500 g equal 1,000 g committed; entering 2,000 g available produces an initial allowance of 3,000 g. Produced quantities remain consumed. Released reservations stay released; a later restoration uses the new mode. Prices, ordered quantities and other series remain unchanged. Conversion and its history save together. If a historic size or reservation cannot be reliably reconstructed, conversion is refused without changes; check sizes and stock history. An order being edited may cause a conflict: reload and retry. Opening, choosing or cancelling writes nothing. Apply immediately saves remaining stock for the displayed series, preserves committed orders and journals the change, without waiting for product Save or carte Publish. After a conflict your values remain visible; use Reload stock to review current quantities before applying again. View and scroll the stock editor From a product, Items or a Carte, the availability editor opens in a large centered dialog. Its position does not depend on where the opening button sits on the page. On desktop, per-size quantities use two columns; narrow screens keep one column. Scroll the content to reach the last sizes or recovery messages: the title, close control, Cancel and Apply stay visible. The dialog fits the available screen height, including mobile landscape. Choices remain a draft until Apply; Cancel or Escape closes without saving and returns focus to the opening button. Choose the stock source and profile With menu editing permission, open a saved product → Stock & availability → Edit stock and availability. The Availability badge in Items or a Carte opens the same editor for current stock. Opening it changes nothing. Choose Available without limit, Unavailable, Manually defined quantity or Quantity calculated from recipe. Manual quantity is the remaining stock entered in units, g/ml or per size; existing commitments remain reserved. Recipe calculation uses available ingredients and preparations and stops applying the manual counter. Old counters and frozen reservations remain intact for existing orders. Without recipe ingredients, no quantity limit can be calculated: a message asks you to complete the recipe. If ready-stock sale is active, disable it in the preparation settings and save the product before choosing recipe calculation. Advanced stock settings start collapsed. Open them to choose the Stock profile. Use the default setting inherits the category profile, then the restaurant profile; a named profile such as Standard is an explicit choice. The profile controls stock tracking, the low-stock threshold, displaying the remaining count and hiding the product or marking it sold out when empty. A summary describes the selected profile. If the profile does not track stock, a visible message says sales are not limited by stock. Available without limit and Unavailable keep priority. The profile belongs to the product across all series; quantities and the stock source apply to the displayed series, or the product stock outside series. Apply directly saves every setting in this dialog: availability, source, tracking mode, unit, quantities and profile. This works with or without series, without product Save. Unsaved names, prices and preparation settings stay independent and are not saved. A profile-only change does not rewrite stock or reservations, including exhausted stock and inactive products. Stock and profile changes submitted together commit in one transaction: failure rolls back both and retains inputs. Dialog controls are locked while saving. Cancel or Escape before applying discards choices; after confirmation, leaving the product does not undo the applied settings. If saving succeeds but refreshing fails, Retry only reloads data without repeating the adjustment. Edit reusable profiles in Settings → Stock → Availability.

articles.title: Kitchen Companion: prep, service and closing
articles.description: Compatible activated iPad → More → Kitchen Companion
articles.body: Compatible activated iPad → More → Kitchen Companion Availability and access Native iPad/tablet layout and kitchen permissions are required; availability depends on activation. Prepare production objectives Review the selected service and proposed production quantities. Adjust allowed objectives and record actual preparation quantities using the corresponding controls. Review service priorities Open the service workspace to review availability and priorities. Treat simulation/projection results as planning aids and verify actual stock before making a production decision. Review sales and close the day Review sales links, counts, variance and preparation results. Save the review and use closing only after checking the figures; do not repeat a confirmed stock-changing closure. Use compatible Siri access On a supported activated iPad with the required system version and permissions, use the configured Siri/App Intents. If unavailable, use the app workspace; this is not Android voice support.

articles.title: Daily Operations
articles.description: Prepare service, review sales and stock, close/reopen a day, and explicitly generate and send supplier drafts.
articles.body: Kitchen → Today → Kitchen companion. Open the correct day Open Kitchen → Today, the Kitchen companion page. Select a date using the calendar and arrows; Today returns to the current day. Check restaurant and open/closed status. A historical day without a report differs from a loading error. Some production and receiving actions are offered only for the current day. Access and required data Changes require kitchen management permission and the relevant report controls. Configure recipes, units, prices and suppliers for useful calculations. Unmatched sales and missing recipes limit consumption/forecast coverage; they do not mean zero consumption. Prepare service In Prepare service, review preparations to launch, targets, sales forecasts and deliveries to check. A forecast is an estimate. Open a preparation and confirm production to record a batch; viewing a target or forecast produces nothing. Unavailable indicators show loading/error states, not reliable zero counts. During service During service compares preparation stock with a target entered for the next service. These targets are a local page simulation, not saved stock counts or supplier orders. Production requires a separate confirmation. Also review the sales journal and ingredients needing replenishment. Import, link and correct sales In Day review, open the journal, Import sales or Manual Sales Entry on an open report. Choose Foody POS or the offered external/Aviv file source, then review rows and item links. Do not manually duplicate sales already pulled from POS. Save manual quantities and check the result; link unmatched external products before interpreting consumption. Check and receive deliveries In Prepare service, Check delivery opens an expected purchase order. Check actually delivered quantities before confirming. Scan/import and quick receiving are separate actions. View recorded receipts in their drawer. Authorized deletion requires confirmation and can reverse the relevant movement; do not credit the same delivery twice through another import. Compare expected and counted stock Day review separates expected stock, physically counted quantities and variance. Use review filters/search, open an ingredient, enter its measured remaining quantity and confirm. Physical counts are optional: a missing count remains uncounted, not zero. Check the unit and saved result. Unmatched sales indicate incomplete coverage. Use the dedicated cost and recipe workspaces The review uses available sales, recipes and movements to explain variance. Cost/margin analysis and recipe imports have dedicated workspaces; do not look for the former charts or a recipe-import button inside this review. Food cost · Recipe Lab · Recipe quantities. Save the handover note Enter the handover note in Day review and use Save Draft after changes. This saves the note and recomputes the report; it does not close the day or send supplier orders. Wait for confirmation before changing date or leaving. Close the day Check sales, mappings and counts, then click Close Day and accept its confirmation. Closing recomputes/freezes the report, applies external/manual consumption not yet deducted and reconciles explicitly counted ingredients. Foody POS sales already deduct stock through the order flow and are not deducted again at close. Closing neither generates nor sends supplier orders. After an uncertain response, refresh and check closed status before another action. Reopen an eligible report Reopen day is offered for an eligible closed report, excluding historical-only imports. After confirmation, the server reverses deductions/count reconciliations belonging to that close and makes the report editable. Review sales/counts, then close again when appropriate. It does not recall supplier emails already sent. Explicitly generate estimated drafts On a closed report, open Estimated Supplies. Click All recorded sales, Aviv and manual sales or From POS to generate. Closing alone does not run generation. The calculation uses history, recipes and stock to suggest shortages grouped by supplier. It creates drafts without sending emails or orders. Review quantities, units and supplier; regeneration replaces previously generated drafts for that report. A forecast remains an estimate; diagnostics distinguish missing history, unlinked recipes and no shortages. Review and manually send Closing or generation never automatically sends a supplier order. Review the draft and requested delivery date; a delivery date/start is required for email. If missing, use the order’s send dialog in Kitchen → Purchases, fill Delivery date and start and complete the manual send there. If the date is already set, Send order in the estimated drawer opens the dialog: check the recipient, then click Send. Only this explicit action triggers email. Check status and result afterward; if uncertain after sending, verify before retrying. Purchases and orders. Recover after an error Distinguish empty results from load failures. If a confirmed save is followed by refresh failure, reload the result instead of repeating receipt, production, close or send. Preserve unsaved input before changing date. If sending remains uncertain, check the order and delivery outcome before transmitting again. Workflow and related guides Prepare service, receive deliveries, review sales/stock, save handover, then close. Separately generate and review supplier drafts; send only after manual confirmation. Stock · Preparations · Delivery import · Purchases. For an item tracked by a shared counter whose rule shows the remaining count, the cart accounts for available quantity even above the low-stock threshold. That threshold controls the warning, not the cart cap. See Availability to check the rule and manual overrides. Check the series stock journal Predefined item stocks now have a journal under Items & menus → Stock history and on each product. A rotating carte can prepare initial allowances per series and publish them without restoring already committed units. Previous remaining counts are not carried forward. Order changes and pre-production releases use the original frozen pool; a produced item remains consumed. Ingredient/preparation quantities and recipe costs remain separate. See Availability for initial imports, corrections and history filters. Identify the variant to prepare For an item with position choices, check the characters and their order on the order and ticket. Kitchen counters distinguish choice combinations so two products with the same format are not confused. Availability and stock movements continue to use the item and its priced format; a descriptive character creates no surcharge or second stock debit.

articles.title: Scan and review supplier deliveries

articles.title: Food cost
articles.description: See the cost and margin of every dish, computed from its recipe, set a target, and find the dishes eating your profit.
articles.body: Open the corresponding Foody workspace described below. What Is It? Food cost tells you what each dish costs you to make and how much margin it leaves — computed automatically from its recipe and your stock prices . It's how you find the dishes quietly eating your profit. How It Works (Simply) The number comes straight from the chain you already set up: Stock prices ─┐ ├─→ Recipe (ingredients + preparations × quantities) ─→ Dish cost ─→ Margin vs its price Prep costs ─┘ So a dish only has a food cost once it has a recipe. No recipe = no cost (and the dish shows as un-costed). What you see Under Kitchen → Food Cost, inspect ingredient cost excluding VAT, selling price, cost percentage and margin for priced dishes. The chart has a 35% reference line; this is not an editable target on this page. Use search, status filter and sorting to inspect dishes. Missing recipe quantities or reliable costs prevent a reliable comparison. How to use it - Sort by food cost % to find your worst offenders first. - A dish costs too much? Adjust its portion or ingredients on the Recipe and cost section, change its price, or substitute a cheaper ingredient. - Prices changed? Update the ingredient in Stock; every dish using it re-costs automatically. Theoretical vs actual The Food cost page is your theoretical cost — what each dish should cost. To compare it against what you actually used (waste, over-portioning, errors), close the day in Daily operations; the variance is where money leaks. For an item tracked by a shared counter whose rule shows the remaining count, the cart accounts for available quantity even above the low-stock threshold. That threshold controls the warning, not the cart cap. See Availability to check the rule and manual overrides. Sale allowance is separate from recipe cost Predefined item stocks now have a journal under Items & menus → Stock history and on each product. A rotating carte can prepare initial allowances per series and publish them without restoring already committed units. Previous remaining counts are not carried forward. Order changes and pre-production releases use the original frozen pool; a produced item remains consumed. Ingredient/preparation quantities and recipe costs remain separate. See Availability for initial imports, corrections and history filters.

articles.title: Preparations
articles.description: Sub-recipes you make in batches (sauces, doughs, marinades) and use across many dishes. Producing a batch credits stock; dishes that use it recover availability automatically.
articles.body: Open the corresponding Foody workspace described below. What Is It? A Preparation is a sub-recipe you make ahead in batches — a sauce, a dough, a marinade, a stock — and then use inside several dishes. Instead of listing raw ingredients on every dish, you point dishes at the preparation. How It Works (Simply) 1. Define the preparation in Kitchen → Preparations : its name, unit, and the raw ingredients one batch consumes (its recipe), plus the yield per batch (how much one batch produces). 2. Produce a batch when you make it. Foody deducts the raw ingredients from Stock and credits the produced quantity to the preparation. 3. Use it in dishes : on a dish's Recipe and cost section, add the preparation as an ingredient with the quantity one portion needs. Because dishes consume the preparation, its current quantity feeds straight into Availability: when a prep hits 0, dishes that use it go sold out — and the moment you produce a new batch, they come back. Why use them - Less duplication — change the sauce recipe once, every dish that uses it follows. - Accurate food cost — the prep's cost per unit rolls up from its ingredients and flows into each dish. - Real availability — "we're out of the green sauce" automatically 86's the right dishes. Example A tahini sauce yields 2 L per batch and costs ₪18 to make. Five dishes use 50 ml each. After producing one batch you can build ~40 portions; when it drops near zero those dishes show low stock , then sold out — until you produce another batch. For an item tracked by a shared counter whose rule shows the remaining count, the cart accounts for available quantity even above the low-stock threshold. That threshold controls the warning, not the cart cap. See Availability to check the rule and manual overrides. Keep preparation stock separate from sale allowances Predefined item stocks now have a journal under Items & menus → Stock history and on each product. A rotating carte can prepare initial allowances per series and publish them without restoring already committed units. Previous remaining counts are not carried forward. Order changes and pre-production releases use the original frozen pool; a produced item remains consumed. Ingredient/preparation quantities and recipe costs remain separate. See Availability for initial imports, corrections and history filters. Identify the variant to prepare For an item with position choices, check the characters and their order on the order and ticket. articles.title: Recipe Lab and version review
articles.description: Admin → Kitchen → Lab
articles.body: Admin → Kitchen → Lab Start or import a recipe Choose manual entry, text import or an offered AI brief. Define the dish/objective, stock policy and relevant quantities before creating a draft. Validate ingredient links Review recipe components, existing/new stock and preparations. Resolve unit conversions and estimated prices; an estimated price is not a confirmed supplier purchase cost. Refine and review cost Use the refinement panel to propose changes, then inspect the recipe tree and cost summary. Verify preparation steps and image proposals before accepting them. Commit a reviewed version Select the intended menu item and commit only a validated draft. Use version history to inspect saved versions; check an uncertain commit before submitting it again.

articles.title: Stock Management
articles.description: Track raw ingredients, manage units and conversions, record transactions, import deliveries with AI, and get alerts when stock runs low.
articles.body: Kitchen → Stock: operational ingredient list, quantities and movements. Read the current stock list Stock shows a search/filter toolbar, Actions, Create item when permitted and an ingredient table. It no longer has the old Total Items, Low Stock and Inventory Value KPI cards. Value is shown per row and on the ingredient record, not in a summary card above the list. Search and filter by category or status Search by name. Category selects categories; Status offers Low Stock and OK. All Filters opens the combined filter panel. Criteria combine. Select Low Stock under Status to isolate ingredients needing restocking. Do not look for the old Low Stock Only checkbox. An empty filtered list is different from a loading error. Read columns and packaging levels The table includes name, category, quantity, price, total row value, supplier and status. Status flags Low Stock when the configured threshold is reached, otherwise showing the appropriate item state. Quantity and Price cells cycle available packaging display levels. This changes presentation, not stock. There is no gear column selector beside this page’s filters. An active ingredient with zero quantity also counts as Low Stock, even without a positive threshold. Create or edit an ingredient record With kitchen management permission, click Create item or open an existing row. The full-screen editor is continuous with a side summary; it does not have the old General and Packaging & Pricing tabs. Work through Identity & purchase, Purchase & price, Units and conversions, reorder threshold and Invoice names. Save commits the record. Enter identity, purchase and price Enter the order name, category, reference and supplier as needed. Under Purchase & price, describe the quantity and packaging actually bought, then the total price and requested VAT information. Supported forms cover a simple quantity, a container with contents, or packages containing multiple units. Check the base-unit summary before Save. Use Actions → price display to change list presentation excluding/including VAT; this does not alter recorded purchases. Understand units and conversions Base quantities use g, kg, ml, l or units. Packaging describes how they are bought: for example, 2 cartons × 12 cans × 400 g = 9.6 kg. Recipes use compatible units. Under Units and conversions, add a custom recipe unit with its equivalent base quantity and verify the conversion. Never infer a container’s contents from its name alone. Record a receipt, waste or adjustment Open the row action menu and choose the movement. Enter a positive quantity in the displayed unit and an optional note. Receive adds it; waste and manual adjustment subtract it. Check current and resulting stock before Confirm. If the movement saved but refresh failed, retry refresh rather than entering a second movement. Read history and understand variance The row History action shows up to 50 recent movements with type, quantity change, note and date. Distinguish receipts, waste and adjustments from consumption created by sales or production. A load error is not empty history. Compare theoretical and actual use for the relevant day in Daily Operations and check recipes and closing counts. Categories, selection and bulk actions Use row checkboxes to select records. Depending on permissions and selection, Actions offers category management, category or VAT updates, deletion and deselection. Category and Status filters limit the visible list; check selected rows before editing multiple records. Deletion confirmation is separate from filtering. Import a delivery and resume a draft From Actions, open Import delivery. Choose the supplier, upload the document and review extracted lines before confirming: matches to existing ingredients, units, packaging, quantities, prices and VAT. Analysis is not a confirmed receipt. Save a draft when needed and resume it from Supplies. Delivery-note import · Suppliers and purchases. Link ingredients to recipes In a saved item, Recipe and cost lets you add raw ingredients or preparations and enter quantities per serving or size. Stock record price and unit feed the calculation. Import a recipe from its recipe import action or Recipe Lab; this is not a bulk action of the Stock list. Recipe quantities · Recipe Lab. Check after changes After saving, check quantity, price, unit, status and effects on affected recipes. If image upload or refresh fails after a record was created, finish that step on the existing record without duplication. Align thresholds with your purchasing cycle and check the day before closing it. Units and stock settings · Daily Operations. Estimated supplies in Day review require explicit draft generation and a manual send; closing or generating does not transmit a supplier order. For an item tracked by a shared counter whose rule shows the remaining count, the cart accounts for available quantity even above the low-stock threshold. That threshold controls the warning, not the cart cap. See Availability to check the rule and manual overrides. Investigate predefined product stock Predefined item stocks now have a journal under Items & menus → Stock history and on each product. A rotating carte can prepare initial allowances per series and publish them without restoring already committed units. Previous remaining counts are not carried forward. Order changes and pre-production releases use the original frozen pool; a produced item remains consumed. Ingredient/preparation quantities and recipe costs remain separate. See Availability for initial imports, corrections and history filters. Identify the variant to prepare For an item with position choices, check the characters and their order on the order and ticket. Kitchen counters distinguish choice combinations so two products with the same format are not confused. Availability and stock movements continue to use the item and its priced format; a descriptive character creates no surcharge or second stock debit.

articles.title: Suppliers and purchase orders
articles.description: Admin → Kitchen → Purchases
articles.body: Admin → Kitchen → Purchases Maintain supplier products Create or edit supplier contact details, then review linked stock products and purchasing units/prices. Save and check the product mapping before ordering. Turn needs into a purchase order Review the Needs view, choose the supplier and adjust proposed quantities. Create the purchase order and check its lines and total before sending. Review and send the order Open the send action, review recipient/channel and the proposed message, then confirm the intended send. Check its result separately from saving the purchase order. For email, fill Delivery date and start before sending; End of delivery window is optional and must be later. Generating or saving a draft does not send it. Verify the recipient and explicitly confirm Send; if the outcome is uncertain, check status before repeating. Receive or cancel deliberately Use Receive for actual delivered quantities and reconcile discrepancies. Cancellation/deletion have different effects; read the confirmation and avoid crediting stock twice through another import.

articles.title: Units, stock policy and availability
articles.description: Open Settings → Stock, Units and Availability. Keep measurement units consistent with recipes and purchasing.
articles.body: Open Settings → Stock, Units and Availability. Keep measurement units consistent with recipes and purchasing. Manage measurement units Review unit names, dimensions and conversions before adding or editing a unit. Use compatible mass, volume or count units; a supplier pack size is not automatically a recipe quantity. Verify existing ingredient and recipe references before deletion. Set stock and availability policy Review when stock is reserved/consumed and how shortages affect public availability. Check the configured policy with a small development scenario before changing service behavior. Manual item visibility, timed availability and ingredient stock are separate restrictions and can combine. For an item tracked by a shared counter whose rule shows the remaining count, the cart accounts for available quantity even above the low-stock threshold. That threshold controls the warning, not the cart cap. See Availability to check the rule and manual overrides. Read quantities in the correct stock pool Predefined item stocks now have a journal under Items & menus → Stock history and on each product. A rotating carte can prepare initial allowances per series and publish them without restoring already committed units. Previous remaining counts are not carried forward. Order changes and pre-production releases use the original frozen pool; a produced item remains consumed. Ingredient/preparation quantities and recipe costs remain separate. See Availability for initial imports, corrections and history filters.

articles.title: Online promotions and discount codes
articles.description: Admin → Clients → Promotions
articles.body: Admin → Clients → Promotions Create a promotion Create the discount code and choose fixed amount or percentage. Review its value, eligible scope, minimum basket and validity dates before saving. Set usage limits Set the available usage/customer restrictions and active state. Check the restaurant timezone when scheduling a start or end date. Verify the guest result Test an eligible basket in the agreed test environment. Verify the discount line and final total; a rejected code should explain the applicable restriction.

articles.title: Stories and Instagram content
articles.description: Open Settings → Stories and the supported social connection controls.
articles.body: Open Settings → Stories and the supported social connection controls. Connect and select content Use the offered authorization flow, select permitted content and check its public visibility. External account permissions and media availability can expire. Reconnect through the protected flow rather than sharing an access token. Verify the stories page Open the restaurant’s public Stories page on mobile and check media, order and links. A social media connection does not automatically publish unrelated Website draft changes. Remove unavailable content using the offered controls.

articles.title: Items, categories and customer menus
articles.description: Understand where to create items and how to make them visible to guests.
articles.body: Items & menus → Item library: catalogue library, filters and actions. Use the Items library Items is a table-based library with search, filters and actions. There are no Total Items or Out of Stock KPI cards above this list. Categories classify the internal catalogue and reporting; they are not the customer menu sections. Search, filter and choose columns Search by name. Category and Status filters combine; Status offers Active and Inactive, with active items selected initially. All Filters opens the filter panel. Calculated availability is separate from active/inactive status. The header column picker controls Images, Category, Availability and Price. Click Name or Price to sort. The list is paginated. Create, edit and apply bulk actions With menu editing permission, click Create item to open the full-screen editor, or click an existing row to edit it. Actions includes imports and refresh. After selecting rows, it also offers category, option and modifier assignment, availability overrides and confirmed deletion. Check the selected items and restaurant before a bulk action. Show an item to customers Carte membership, groups, order, channels and hours now use a private draft: Save draft, Preview, then explicit Publish. Shared product details remain in the item library. On a publication-managed carte, choose item membership from the carte draft instead of the product group picker. Initial quantities for a rotating series are prepared separately from live recipe/ingredient stock. See Menus and groups and Availability for preparation, history and recovery. Choose groups in the carte draft Carte membership, groups, order, channels and hours now use a private draft: Save draft, Preview, then explicit Publish. Shared product details remain in the item library. On a publication-managed carte, choose item membership from the carte draft instead of the product group picker. Initial quantities for a rotating series are prepared separately from live recipe/ingredient stock. See Menus and groups and Availability for preparation, history and recovery. Access the new controls Carte availability is now directly clickable beneath an item name. When the sale allowance is exhausted, enter the remaining quantity; committed orders are preserved. Review the availability procedure before changing sale stock. Change availability from Items With menu editing permission, open a saved product → Stock & availability → Edit stock and availability. The Availability badge in Items or a Carte opens the same editor for current stock. Opening it changes nothing. Choose Available without limit, Unavailable, Manually defined quantity or Quantity calculated from recipe. Manual quantity is the remaining stock entered in units, g/ml or per size; existing commitments remain reserved. Recipe calculation uses available ingredients and preparations and stops applying the manual counter. Old counters and frozen reservations remain intact for existing orders. Without recipe ingredients, no quantity limit can be calculated: a message asks you to complete the recipe. If ready-stock sale is active, disable it in the preparation settings and save the product before choosing recipe calculation. Apply directly saves every setting in this dialog: availability, source, tracking mode, unit, quantities and profile. This works with or without series, without product Save. Unsaved names, prices and preparation settings stay independent and are not saved. A profile-only change does not rewrite stock or reservations, including exhausted stock and inactive products. Stock and profile changes submitted together commit in one transaction: failure rolls back both and retains inputs. Dialog controls are locked while saving. Cancel or Escape before applying discards choices; after confirmation, leaving the product does not undo the applied settings. If saving succeeds but refreshing fails, Retry only reloads data without repeating the adjustment. Edit reusable profiles in Settings → Stock → Availability. Within a carte draft, applied stock replaces only this item’s stock preparation; other drafts stay private. Stock loads freshly on opening. On conflict, reload, review quantities and explicitly apply again. Check conditional item choices An item configured with repeated positions requires one separate choice per position according to the selected format. For example, a two-character Number Cake accepts 11, AB or A7. The format price replaces the base price; modifiers add only their configured surcharges. Reducing the position count removes newly hidden choices. Positions remain distinct in the cart, orders and kitchen ticket; review them before confirming. These customizations do not change delivery, availability, recipe, discount or cancellation rules. Configuration requires compatible versions and menu editing permission. See Variants and sizes for setup and recovery after a rejected selection. Browse the library on mobile On a handheld terminal, open Library. The filter button selects Items, Combos or Discounts. Under Items, choose a category in the selector above the list, search for a product and tap its row to open the existing editor. Price and availability remain visible, with a separate switch for authorized users. This internal list does not change published menu groups, ingredients, portions or variant rules configured in Admin. Product photos An item can show several photos. See Product photos for adding photos, selecting the cover and using the dots, arrows or horizontal swipe in product details. A single photo has no gallery controls. Choose units and shared or per-size stock With menu editing permission, open a series-tracked product → Stock & availability → Edit stock and availability, or the Availability badge in Items or a Carte. Select Manually defined quantity. Choose the tracking mode, including for a series that already has committed orders: Shared unit count deducts one per item; Shared measure pools a budget across sizes; Count per size keeps an independent counter for each variant. Compatible numeric sizes offer g/kg or ml/l under Input unit. For example, 2,000 g in shared measure is shared between the 250 g and 500 g sizes. In count per size, entering 1,000 g for each allows 4 portions of 250 g and 2 portions of 500 g, with no sharing between counters. Check the displayed equivalents: each per-size budget must equal a whole number of portions. A blank size remains unlimited; enter 0 to exhaust it, with at least one other positive size. Use Unavailable to exhaust the whole item. Changing g to kg or ml to l preserves the quantity; changing tracking mode clears the fields to avoid converting portions into grams. When the mode changes, existing reservations are recalculated from each ordered size and added to the remaining quantity you enter: 2 portions of 250 g and 1 of 500 g equal 1,000 g committed; entering 2,000 g available produces an initial allowance of 3,000 g. Produced quantities remain consumed. Released reservations stay released; a later restoration uses the new mode. Prices, ordered quantities and other series remain unchanged. Conversion and its history save together. If a historic size or reservation cannot be reliably reconstructed, conversion is refused without changes; check sizes and stock history. An order being edited may cause a conflict: reload and retry. Opening, choosing or cancelling writes nothing. Apply immediately saves remaining stock for the displayed series, preserves committed orders and journals the change, without waiting for product Save or carte Publish. After a conflict your values remain visible; use Reload stock to review current quantities before applying again. View and scroll the stock editor From a product, Items or a Carte, the availability editor opens in a large centered dialog. Its position does not depend on where the opening button sits on the page. On desktop, per-size quantities use two columns; narrow screens keep one column. Scroll the content to reach the last sizes or recovery messages: the title, close control, Cancel and Apply stay visible. The dialog fits the available screen height, including mobile landscape. Choices remain a draft until Apply; Cancel or Escape closes without saving and returns focus to the opening button. Choose the stock source and profile With menu editing permission, open a saved product → Stock & availability → Edit stock and availability. The Availability badge in Items or a Carte opens the same editor for current stock. Opening it changes nothing. Choose Available without limit, Unavailable, Manually defined quantity or Quantity calculated from recipe. Manual quantity is the remaining stock entered in units, g/ml or per size; existing commitments remain reserved. Recipe calculation uses available ingredients and preparations and stops applying the manual counter. Old counters and frozen reservations remain intact for existing orders. Without recipe ingredients, no quantity limit can be calculated: a message asks you to complete the recipe. If ready-stock sale is active, disable it in the preparation settings and save the product before choosing recipe calculation. Advanced stock settings start collapsed. Open them to choose the Stock profile. Use the default setting inherits the category profile, then the restaurant profile; a named profile such as Standard is an explicit choice. The profile controls stock tracking, the low-stock threshold, displaying the remaining count and hiding the product or marking it sold out when empty. A summary describes the selected profile. If the profile does not track stock, a visible message says sales are not limited by stock. Available without limit and Unavailable keep priority. The profile belongs to the product across all series; quantities and the stock source apply to the displayed series, or the product stock outside series. Apply directly saves every setting in this dialog: availability, source, tracking mode, unit, quantities and profile. This works with or without series, without product Save. Unsaved names, prices and preparation settings stay independent and are not saved. A profile-only change does not rewrite stock or reservations, including exhausted stock and inactive products. Stock and profile changes submitted together commit in one transaction: failure rolls back both and retains inputs. Dialog controls are locked while saving. Cancel or Escape before applying discards choices; after confirmation, leaving the product does not undo the applied settings. If saving succeeds but refreshing fails, Retry only reloads data without repeating the adjustment. Edit reusable profiles in Settings → Stock → Availability.

articles.title: Combos and configurable formulas
articles.description: Item editor → combo configuration / POS combo entry
articles.body: Item editor → combo configuration / POS combo entry Define the formula steps Create the formula steps and eligible item choices. Set each step’s selection/quantity rules and review which variants/options can be configured. Review formula pricing Review base/formula prices and choice supplements in the pricing preview. Verify the resulting basket for several allowed combinations instead of assuming every choice has the same price. Take a combo order Select the combo and complete every required step. On a compact terminal with limited available width, Cancel Combo and Previous Step occupy the first row; Next Step or Add to order spans the row below. Previous Step appears after the first step. Next Step remains unavailable while the current choice is incomplete; Add requires every step to be satisfied. Scroll the grid to reach further choices. Review components, note and price before adding; an eligible existing-line edit is confirmed with Done. Cancel discards provisional choices without adding the combo. Tablets and sufficiently wide areas retain a single row of buttons. This adaptation changes neither selection limits, surcharges nor permissions. Check kitchen presentation separately on the intended channel. Make a one-order combo exception With orders.manage permission, open New order or edit a saved order in Admin and open its combo composition. In the relevant step, select Choose another item. Remove one selected unit first if the step is full, search the restaurant article library and choose the replacement and its size. Exception · included identifies the choice. Active fixed-price individual items are eligible, including items outside the active carte; inactive, sold-out and weight-priced items and other combos cannot be used. Required step quantities, per-item limits and configured portions still apply. Save the combo, review the ticket and submit once. For example, replace the beef in a two-main Mamie formula with fish while retaining chicken. The replacement and its size add no surcharge; other normal configured choices keep their existing surcharges. The formula base price and saved definition do not change, and editing an existing order preserves its original base-price snapshot. The choice survives draft restoration and reopening the order editor. Guests cannot request this exception. If rejected, refresh availability and choose an active item in an allowed size; a failed saved-order replacement retains the previous composition. Build a combo on the restaurant website Open a combo in the website menu. Its sheet uses the item-detail color style, site fonts, corners and button shape. Choose the quantity when offered, then Build your combo. The catalogue keeps its presentation throughout composition; only eligible, available items for the current step can be selected. Tap an item, then choose a variant if requested. The counter shows your picks; the − button removes a pick. Previous step lets you review a choice, and View details opens the sheet without clearing the composition. Complete the steps and add the combo to the cart. Cancel leaves composition without adding a combo. A fixed combo lists its contents and adds directly from its sheet. If a choice is disabled, check its step membership and availability. For incorrect colors, check the item-detail style assigned in the order page and publish the reviewed settings.

articles.title: Creating a Menu Item, Step by Step
articles.description: End-to-end walkthrough of creating a new menu item in FoodyAdmin: image, name, description, category, price, variants, recipe, and cost.
articles.body: Items & menus → Item library → Create item opens the continuous full-screen editor. Check access and open the editor Check the active restaurant and your menu editing permission. Open Items & menus → Item library and click Create item. This is one continuous full-screen form: scroll through its sections. It does not use the old three-tab Details, Recipe and Cost modal. Save stays available in the header. Item information and photos Choose the item type, name and description. Add photo accepts several image files, up to 10 photos of 5 MB each. Open a thumbnail to choose the primary photo or remove it, then Save. See Product photos for supported formats, website dots and recovery. Translation editing is available for saved items. Shared product details remain in the item library. On a publication-managed carte, choose item membership from the carte draft instead of the product group picker. On wide screens the side cards appear on the right in French and English and on the left in Hebrew; below 1024 px they follow the form. A by-weight item requires its per-kilogram price and the requested estimated weight. Variant prices are absolute and replace the base price; modifier prices are additional amounts. Portion describes serving size; it does not automatically fill recipe ingredient quantities. Customer information contains customer-facing facts. Stock & availability and Recipe and cost follow on the same page. AI assistant context is private guidance for the ordering assistant, separate from support. A combo uses Composition instead of the standard item recipe sections. Save, then complete the recipe Click Save. Before the first save, Recipe and cost and Stock & availability offer to save and configure because these settings require a created item. Reopen it and scroll to Recipe and cost. Ingredient edits save immediately; recipe instructions and notes save with the item. Wait for confirmation and retry an error without creating another item. Verify visibility and resolve a missing item Check group membership, menu/group channels, hours and availability, then inspect the relevant website or POS. If Save is disabled, check permission, name and required price. If creation is only partially complete, keep the editor and retry the remaining steps rather than recreating the item. articles.title: How to Configure Ingredients & Portions
articles.description: Configure ingredient quantities per serving or size, units, prefill and cost in the Recipe and cost section.

After adding, check its row, quantity and save confirmation. A preparation needs a yield and cost for a reliable calculation. Enter quantity for one serving Without different quantities per size, enter each ingredient quantity for one serving in a compatible unit. Example: 200 g beef, one bun and 20 g sauce. A missing value is not an automatically calculated quantity. Resolve validation errors before continuing. Set quantities per size For an item with variants, enable different quantities per size. Check every size: an ingredient with no quantity for a variant is not deducted for that variant until corrected. Do not look for an automatic Scale to item size mode instead of entering these cells. Check units, cost and modifiers Use units compatible with stock and configure custom recipe-unit conversions on the stock record when needed. The table derives ingredient cost excluding VAT and per-variant totals from entered quantities. Investigate a missing or zero cost on the stock/preparation record instead of treating the recipe as free. Configure add-ons through modifier groups; their price does not fill base recipe quantities. Save and recover from an error Ingredient edits save immediately; instructions and notes save with the item. An error retains input: retry before leaving and verify the result. If an ingredient record was created but linking it failed, find that record and complete the link without creating a duplicate. Stock · Variants. articles.title: Menus and groups (what customers see)
articles.description: How items, categories, menus (cartes) and groups differ, how to control what shows online vs on the POS, and the availability hours for each.
articles.body: Items & menus → Menus: open a menu, then create or edit its groups. What Is It?
