Foody separates what you sell from how you show it — the same idea Square uses, so the catalogue works for any business. - Items — your global catalogue of dishes/products (created once). - Categories — internal labels for you (reporting, kitchen routing). Customers never see categories. - Menus (cartes) — a customer-facing menu, e.g. "Breakfast", "Lunch", "Dinner". - Groups — the visual sections inside a menu, e.g. "Salads", "Drinks". This is what customers see. The rule that trips everyone up: an item must be placed in a group to appear to customers. Being in a category is not enough — categories are internal only. The structure Item (global catalogue — "Caesar Salad") └─ belongs to one Category (internal: "Salads") ← customers don't see this Menu / carte ("Lunch") └─ Group ("Salads") ← customers DO see this └─ contains Items (the same item can sit in several groups/menus) A group like "Lunch specials" can pull items from several categories. The same item can appear in several groups and menus. Check menu tabs on the website Two menus, such as BASSARI and HALAVI, remain separate menus. On an order page offering several visible menus, tabs select one menu at a time. Category menu pills represent groups within that menu, such as Sandwiches, rather than internal library categories. Enable each menu’s Web channel, select them in the order page settings, then check both navigation levels in preview and after publishing. Group navigation styling lives in Item list. See website menu and group navigation. Prepare, save and publish a carte Open Items & menus → Menus and select the carte. For a rotating carte, choose its series in the header. Add lets you choose items for a group or create a group; Add menu group is also available below the list. A group’s chevron collapses or expands its table without changing the carte. Its “…” menu contains Edit group and Choose items. The “…” menu beside the carte title contains Carte settings and Preview. Group, channel and hours edits stay local. Once edits or a saved draft exist, the bottom bar offers Save draft and Publish. Save stores a private draft; Preview opens a private list that cannot take orders. Publish asks for confirmation and applies the carte and prepared stocks together. Saving alone never changes the live website or POS. Edit POS layout opens the separate tile editor; unsaved changes are guarded before navigating there. Choose items with photos and filters Inside a carte group, click Add items or … → Choose items. Add or remove items shows each product photo, or an icon when no image can be displayed, and the variant count when there is more than one. The trailing checkboxes add or remove group membership in the draft only; they never delete library records. The count includes selected items hidden by filters. Search combines with Filters → Category: select one or more internal categories, then Apply. The target group is separate from the category; from Add → Add items, choose it in Menu group. Menu and Stock filters also combine; Stock offers All stock, Low stock alert and Out of stock using the calculated availability for the selected series. Point of sale is limited to the active restaurant. Clear removes choices in the open filter; Apply confirms them. Closing that filter or pressing Escape discards unapplied choices. Clear all filters restores the full list without changing checked items or the search. If nothing matches, adjust the search or clear filters. A category loading failure offers Retry; it is not an empty category. Done closes the picker and keeps local edits; then Save draft and explicitly Publish. Create a new item opens the shared item editor and first protects unsaved carte changes. Where it sells: online vs POS Each menu and group has channel switches: - Web enabled — shows in the online / QR ordering app for guests. - POS enabled — shows on the staff POS. So you can run, say, a "Dinner" menu that's web-only, or hide a group from guests but keep it on the POS. Turn a group off for one channel and it simply doesn't appear there. When it sells: availability hours A menu (and each group) can follow your opening hours or use custom hours — e.g. a "Breakfast" group that only shows 07:00–11:00. Outside its hours, customers don't see it. How this connects to availability Channels and hours determine whether a group can be shown. Item availability can then make it orderable, sold out or hidden, depending on its rule and manual status. A sold-out item may remain visible with a badge; membership in a group does not guarantee it is orderable. Availability. Check the publication Create and save the shared library items first. Add them to the carte draft, check the selected series, web/POS channels, hours and group hiding, then preview and publish. The current series stays unchanged while preparing a future series. A future series without a publication is not served once carte publication is activated. Product names, prices, recipes and active status remain shared library edits; availability switches marked immediate apply immediately and are journaled. Leave safely and resolve a conflict If you leave or change series with unsaved edits, choose Save draft and leave, Discard, or Continue editing. Discard in this dialog drops unsaved edits only; a previously saved draft remains. Discard draft on the carte removes the saved draft after confirmation and keeps the published carte live. If saving or publishing fails, stay in the editor and review the error. Your edits remain available. A stale revision, changed stock setting, invalid quantity or allowance below existing commitments prevents publication. Reload saved draft explicitly to recover the latest server version; it discards unsaved local edits. Prepare stock for a new series With menu editing permission, open the rotating carte, select a series and open the “…” menu beside the title → Prepare stocks for this series. Enter INITIAL allowances including quantities already ordered: available = initial minus committed. Use shared units, compatible base measures (g/ml), counts per size, or no predefined limit. Copy previous initial quantities copies allowances, never previous remaining quantities or an old sold-out override. Quantities are shared by the same restaurant item across cartes for that series. Save draft keeps preparation private; Publish applies it atomically without restoring reservations made while editing. The first activation imports current available stock and existing scheduled orders, preserving current remaining quantities. Later series never inherit the old global counter. No predefined limit may still be constrained by a recipe, rule or manual status. Use the table and item actions With menu editing permission, select one or more items in a group. The selection bar lets you move them to another group or remove them from this group. A row’s “…” menu also offers Move up, Move down and Remove from group. Dragging reorders rows and groups. These actions edit the draft without deleting shared library items. An item name opens its shared item editor; Select under Modifiers also opens the shared editor; use its Personalizations section to change them. Returning from the editor brings you back to the carte. Leaving unsaved changes offers save, discard or continue editing. Columns show the location, configured channels, modifiers and price; an Availability column reuses the Articles page badges, with remaining stock below each badge. Configured channels do not guarantee ordering: hours, active status and availability still apply. On mobile, secondary columns are hidden while name, stock, price and the “…” menu remain accessible. Change availability and read history With menu editing permission, open a saved product → Stock & availability → Edit stock and availability. The Availability badge in Items or a Carte opens the same editor for current stock. Opening it changes nothing. Choose Available without limit, Unavailable, Manually defined quantity or Quantity calculated from recipe. Manual quantity is the remaining stock entered in units, g/ml or per size; existing commitments remain reserved. Recipe calculation uses available ingredients and preparations and stops applying the manual counter. Old counters and frozen reservations remain intact for existing orders. Without recipe ingredients, no quantity limit can be calculated: a message asks you to complete the recipe. If ready-stock sale is active, disable it in the preparation settings and save the product before choosing recipe calculation. Apply directly saves every setting in this dialog: availability, source, tracking mode, unit, quantities and profile. This works with or without series, without product Save. Unsaved names, prices and preparation settings stay independent and are not saved. A profile-only change does not rewrite stock or reservations, including exhausted stock and inactive products. Stock and profile changes submitted together commit in one transaction: failure rolls back both and retains inputs. Dialog controls are locked while saving. Cancel or Escape before applying discards choices; after confirmation, leaving the product does not undo the applied settings. If saving succeeds but refreshing fails, Retry only reloads data without repeating the adjustment. Edit reusable profiles in Settings → Stock → Availability. Within a carte draft, applied stock replaces only this item’s stock preparation; other drafts stay private. Stock loads freshly on opening. On conflict, reload, review quantities and explicitly apply again. View the stock history journal Open Items & menus → Stock history. This page contains only the movement journal, visible as soon as it opens: it does not list current stock or offer corrections. Choose an Item or All Items, a Series date or All series, and a Movement or All movements. Past series dates are accepted. Filters combine and remain applied when using Show more. The journal shows the date and series, item, movement, before/after quantities and actor; a link opens the associated order when present. An empty result means no movements were recorded for those filters. Initial imports are labeled as imports; changes before tracking was activated cannot be reconstructed. If the item filter fails, Retry reloads that filter while the journal remains available. On a product, the Stock history button opens a dedicated dialog containing only that item’s movements, across all series. On a carte, the row History shortcut or its “…” menu also opens that dialog. To prepare or adjust initial series quantities, open the carte, choose the series, then Prepare stocks for this series, save the draft and publish after reviewing it. Availability actions marked immediate remain separate and journaled. A pre-production cancellation credits the original pool; a produced item remains consumed. If the journal fails to load, Retry reloads movements without changing filters; this error is not presented as an empty history. Change availability from Items With menu editing permission, open a saved product → Stock & availability → Edit stock and availability. The Availability badge in Items or a Carte opens the same editor for current stock. Opening it changes nothing. Choose Available without limit, Unavailable, Manually defined quantity or Quantity calculated from recipe. Manual quantity is the remaining stock entered in units, g/ml or per size; existing commitments remain reserved. Recipe calculation uses available ingredients and preparations and stops applying the manual counter. Old counters and frozen reservations remain intact for existing orders. Without recipe ingredients, no quantity limit can be calculated: a message asks you to complete the recipe. If ready-stock sale is active, disable it in the preparation settings and save the product before choosing recipe calculation. Apply directly saves every setting in this dialog: availability, source, tracking mode, unit, quantities and profile. This works with or without series, without product Save. Unsaved names, prices and preparation settings stay independent and are not saved. A profile-only change does not rewrite stock or reservations, including exhausted stock and inactive products. Stock and profile changes submitted together commit in one transaction: failure rolls back both and retains inputs. Dialog controls are locked while saving. Cancel or Escape before applying discards choices; after confirmation, leaving the product does not undo the applied settings. If saving succeeds but refreshing fails, Retry only reloads data without repeating the adjustment. Edit reusable profiles in Settings → Stock → Availability. Within a carte draft, applied stock replaces only this item’s stock preparation; other drafts stay private. Stock loads freshly on opening. On conflict, reload, review quantities and explicitly apply again. Check conditional item choices An item configured with repeated positions requires one separate choice per position according to the selected format. For example, a two-character Number Cake accepts 11, AB or A7. The format price replaces the base price; modifiers add only their configured surcharges. Reducing the position count removes newly hidden choices. Positions remain distinct in the cart, orders and kitchen ticket; review them before confirming. These customizations do not change delivery, availability, recipe, discount or cancellation rules. Configuration requires compatible versions and menu editing permission. See Variants and sizes for setup and recovery after a rejected selection. Browse the library on mobile On a handheld terminal, open Library. The filter button selects Items, Combos or Discounts. Under Items, choose a category in the selector above the list, search for a product and tap its row to open the existing editor. Price and availability remain visible, with a separate switch for authorized users. This internal list does not change published menu groups, ingredients, portions or variant rules configured in Admin. Choose units and shared or per-size stock With menu editing permission, open a series-tracked product → Stock & availability → Edit stock and availability, or the Availability badge in Items or a Carte. Select Manually defined quantity. Choose the tracking mode, including for a series that already has committed orders: Shared unit count deducts one per item; Shared measure pools a budget across sizes; Count per size keeps an independent counter for each variant. Compatible numeric sizes offer g/kg or ml/l under Input unit. For example, 2,000 g in shared measure is shared between the 250 g and 500 g sizes. In count per size, entering 1,000 g for each allows 4 portions of 250 g and 2 portions of 500 g, with no sharing between counters. Check the displayed equivalents: each per-size budget must equal a whole number of portions. A blank size remains unlimited; enter 0 to exhaust it, with at least one other positive size. Use Unavailable to exhaust the whole item. Changing g to kg or ml to l preserves the quantity; changing tracking mode clears the fields to avoid converting portions into grams. When the mode changes, existing reservations are recalculated from each ordered size and added to the remaining quantity you enter: 2 portions of 250 g and 1 of 500 g equal 1,000 g committed; entering 2,000 g available produces an initial allowance of 3,000 g. Produced quantities remain consumed. Released reservations stay released; a later restoration uses the new mode. Prices, ordered quantities and other series remain unchanged. Conversion and its history save together. If a historic size or reservation cannot be reliably reconstructed, conversion is refused without changes; check sizes and stock history. An order being edited may cause a conflict: reload and retry. Opening, choosing or cancelling writes nothing. Apply immediately saves remaining stock for the displayed series, preserves committed orders and journals the change, without waiting for product Save or carte Publish. After a conflict your values remain visible; use Reload stock to review current quantities before applying again. View and scroll the stock editor From a product, Items or a Carte, the availability editor opens in a large centered dialog. Its position does not depend on where the opening button sits on the page. On desktop, per-size quantities use two columns; narrow screens keep one column. Scroll the content to reach the last sizes or recovery messages: the title, close control, Cancel and Apply stay visible. The dialog fits the available screen height, including mobile landscape. Choices remain a draft until Apply; Cancel or Escape closes without saving and returns focus to the opening button. Choose the stock source and profile With menu editing permission, open a saved product → Stock & availability → Edit stock and availability. The Availability badge in Items or a Carte opens the same editor for current stock. Opening it changes nothing. Choose Available without limit, Unavailable, Manually defined quantity or Quantity calculated from recipe. Manual quantity is the remaining stock entered in units, g/ml or per size; existing commitments remain reserved. Recipe calculation uses available ingredients and preparations and stops applying the manual counter. Old counters and frozen reservations remain intact for existing orders. Without recipe ingredients, no quantity limit can be calculated: a message asks you to complete the recipe. If ready-stock sale is active, disable it in the preparation settings and save the product before choosing recipe calculation. Advanced stock settings start collapsed. Open them to choose the Stock profile. Use the default setting inherits the category profile, then the restaurant profile; a named profile such as Standard is an explicit choice. The profile controls stock tracking, the low-stock threshold, displaying the remaining count and hiding the product or marking it sold out when empty. A summary describes the selected profile. If the profile does not track stock, a visible message says sales are not limited by stock. Available without limit and Unavailable keep priority. The profile belongs to the product across all series; quantities and the stock source apply to the displayed series, or the product stock outside series. Apply directly saves every setting in this dialog: availability, source, tracking mode, unit, quantities and profile. This works with or without series, without product Save. Unsaved names, prices and preparation settings stay independent and are not saved. A profile-only change does not rewrite stock or reservations, including exhausted stock and inactive products. Stock and profile changes submitted together commit in one transaction: failure rolls back both and retains inputs. Dialog controls are locked while saving. Cancel or Escape before applying discards choices; after confirmation, leaving the product does not undo the applied settings. If saving succeeds but refreshing fails, Retry only reloads data without repeating the adjustment. Edit reusable profiles in Settings → Stock → Availability.

articles.title: Modifiers and selection rules
articles.description: Create modifier groups that let customers customize items: add-ons, removals, and options with price adjustments.
articles.body: Admin → Items & menus → Modifier Sets Create a reusable group Create a named option/modifier group and add its choices. Set required/optional selection and allowed minimum/maximum counts, then save. Show POS modifier operators In Admin → Items & menus → Modifier Sets, open the group and Settings. Use conversational modifiers in POS is off by default. Off: only the group’s values appear, without the Add, Extra, No and other operator palette. On: both the handheld terminal and iPad show the colored operators allowed by Verbs shown; an empty list retains all verbs. Choose an operator and then a value. Save the group, then reload the POS catalogue before checking a new item editor: on mobile, open Overview with the house and pull to refresh; on iPad, fully relaunch FoodyPOS outside an ongoing operation. An already open editor does not update instantly. This group setting is separate from an item’s quick-entry setting, which controls opening customization and does not enable the palette. Republishing the menu is not required for this group setting. Set price adjustments Enter modifier price deltas relative to the item price. Variant prices are absolute replacements; do not use the two interchangeably. Options is a separate library entry; see Variants and sizes for size sets and their absolute prices. Link groups to items Open the item editor, attach the reusable groups and order the choices. Verify defaults, selection limits and the final cart price on each enabled channel. Configure guest notes Where a choice offers a customer-note prompt, configure its label/requirement and test the guest form. Guest-only prompts do not require staff to complete the same fields. Shared choices and carte publication Carte membership, groups, order, channels and hours now use a private draft: Save draft, Preview, then explicit Publish. Shared product details remain in the item library. On a publication-managed carte, choose item membership from the carte draft instead of the product group picker. Initial quantities for a rotating series are prepared separately from live recipe/ingredient stock. See Menus and groups and Availability for preparation, history and recovery. Access the new controls Carte availability is now directly clickable beneath an item name. When the sale allowance is exhausted, enter the remaining quantity; committed orders are preserved. Review the availability procedure before changing sale stock. Change availability from Items The Items library Availability column also opens the small panel shared with Cartes. Choose a status or remaining stock and Apply; simply opening it changes nothing. The current series is displayed when applicable. See Categories and items for choices, per-size quantities, cancellation and error recovery. Full item settings retain their own Save action. Condition actual modifier groups Conditions remain available for actual modifiers, such as offering an extra only for a particular format. In the item, under Customizations, attach the group and open Conditions and display. Under Show this group according to, choose an independent priced format or an independent single-choice modifier group. Set its position count per choice: 0 or an unlisted choice hides the group, 1 shows it once, and 2–12 creates required single-choice positions. Save within this panel; these rules apply only to this item. Prices remain deltas added to the item or format price. Sources cannot themselves be conditional; remove dependent conditions before detaching one. For Number Cake characters use option groups under Variants and sizes, preserving their role as variant dimensions without surcharges. Existing modifier groups are not converted automatically.

articles.title: Staff discount library
articles.description: Admin → Articles and menus → Staff discounts
articles.body: Admin → Items & menus → POS discounts Create a named discount Create a name and choose fixed amount, fixed percentage, variable amount or variable percentage. Enter a value for fixed definitions and save the active state. Apply with permission Select an active staff discount on the POS and enter the value when variable. Review eligible check/item scope and final balance before confirming. Distinguish online codes This staff library is separate from guest promotional codes. Do not assume that a staff discount is redeemable online or available to every employee.

articles.title: Manage product photos
articles.description: Items & menus → Item library → open or create an item, then use Add photo.
articles.body: Items & menus → Item library → open or create an item, then use Add photo. Availability and access Select the correct restaurant. Adding or changing photos requires menu editing permission. Add several photos In the item editor, choose Add photo and select one or several JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP files. An item can have up to 10 photos, at most 5 MB each. Thumbnails show their order. On an existing item, uploading files prepares them in the editor; click Save to apply the gallery. On a new item, files upload when you save. Selecting files alone does not save the gallery. A selection exceeding the limit or containing an unsupported file is rejected before uploading. Choose the cover or remove a photo The first photo is marked Primary and remains the cover in product lists and the POS. Open another thumbnail and choose Use as primary photo to move it first. Use Remove image on a thumbnail or its preview to remove it from the product. Removing the first photo promotes the next one. Save applies the changes; Cancel and discard leaves the saved gallery intact. The explicit AI image confirmation still saves the generated cover immediately; additional saved photos remain. Browse the gallery on the customer website Open the product details on the customer website. With several photos, dots below the image show how many are available and which one is selected. Tap a dot or an arrow, swipe horizontally, or focus the gallery and use the arrow keys. Navigation follows the page direction in Hebrew. Reopening a product starts on its cover. A single photo has no gallery controls. The gallery changes neither availability nor the required item choices. Products still need a published web-enabled menu group to appear. Recover from a failed upload or save If an existing item upload fails partway, successfully uploaded photos stay in the editor. Select only the failed files again, then Save. If saving a new item fails during uploads, keep the editor open and retry Save: completed uploads and the created item are reused. If saving the item fails, the form and gallery remain available to retry. Leaving or reloading before Save can lose pending photo selections; local text draft recovery does not restore selected image files. Check the saved item after an interrupted connection before creating another one.

articles.title: Variants & Sizes
articles.description: Set up size or flavor variants on a menu item, with per-variant price, portion, and stock status.
articles.body: Open an item and use Price and variants in its editor. Understand price and portion A variant describes a size or version of an item. Its price is an absolute amount replacing the base price; modifiers are additional amounts. Portion describes serving size. Ingredient quantities are entered separately under Recipe and cost, per serving or variant. Add and save variants Open the item from Items & menus → Item library and scroll to Price and variants. Edit groups and rows directly in this section. Add a set if needed, enter its title and use Add variant for each size. Fill Name, Price, Portion and Status, then Save in the item header. Do not look for the old Details tab or a Done button to commit all variants. Availability, order and combo-only rows Status offers Available and Unavailable. Arrows reorder rows; the bin removes a row and Remove detaches the group from the item. Combo-only marks rows not sold on their own. Check order and prices before Save. Past orders retain their own sale snapshots. Reuse a saved option set Click Saved option sets on the relevant group, search and select a set in the picker. Typing a matching group title alone does not apply a set. Review imported rows, prices, portions and status, then save the item. Check other affected items before changing a shared library. Connect sizes to the recipe Under Recipe and cost, enable different quantities per size and fill the variant columns. Example: 200 g meat for Regular and 400 g for Large, with Same quantity for an identical bun. For soup, explicitly enter 250 ml and 500 ml in the columns; Portion text alone does not supply those quantities. Check missing-quantity warnings. Check after saving Reopen the item to check saved rows, then inspect the enabled POS or web channel. If saving fails, retain the input and retry before closing. Create an item · Recipe quantities. Track size stock by series Carte membership, groups, order, channels and hours now use a private draft: Save draft, Preview, then explicit Publish. Shared product details remain in the item library. On a publication-managed carte, choose item membership from the carte draft instead of the product group picker. Initial quantities for a rotating series are prepared separately from live recipe/ingredient stock. See Menus and groups and Availability for preparation, history and recovery. Access the new controls Carte availability is now directly clickable beneath an item name. When the sale allowance is exhausted, enter the remaining quantity; committed orders are preserved. Review the availability procedure before changing sale stock. Change availability from Items The Items library Availability column also opens the small panel shared with Cartes. Choose a status or remaining stock and Apply; simply opening it changes nothing. The current series is displayed when applicable. See Categories and items for choices, per-size quantities, cancellation and error recovery. Full item settings retain their own Save action. Check conditional item choices An item configured with repeated positions requires one separate choice per position according to the selected format. For example, a two-character Number Cake accepts 11, AB or A7. The format price replaces the base price; modifiers add only their configured surcharges. Reducing the position count removes newly hidden choices. Positions remain distinct in the cart, orders and kitchen ticket; review them before confirming. These customizations do not change delivery, availability, recipe, discount or cancellation rules. Configuration requires compatible versions and menu editing permission. See Variants and sizes for setup and recovery after a rejected selection. Configure Number Cake option positions With menu editing permission and compatible API, Admin, web and POS versions, open the item under Price and variants. Create a Format group with Determines the price: for example 1 character at €55 and 2 characters at €110. Save the item so these choices can be used as a condition source. Add a Character group and choose Describes the variant. Use Add digits and letters to append missing 0–9 and A–Z choices, or enter your own. Under Show this group according to, choose Format and enter 1 and 2 Positions to complete for its two choices. Select Letters and digits under Choice display for the searchable grid, then Save in the item header. Roles and conditions apply to this item only. Each visible position requires exactly one choice: 11, AB and A7 are possible. Characters are not modifiers and do not change the format price; keep actual additions and removals under Customizations. 0 or an unlisted format hides the group. Up to 12 positions are supported; items with these dimensions use at most one independent price-bearing group. The source cannot itself be a conditional dimension. Position choices are offered for standalone items; combo component pickers do not offer them. Weight-priced items cannot use this configuration. Existing catalogs are not converted automatically. If this item already has separate priced Letters and Digits groups, detach them from this item or combine their choices into the Character dimension: keep one priced Format and one group containing both digits and letters. Existing one-character and two-character items are not merged automatically. Check choices and recover a valid configuration Test every format before offering the item: leave a position empty, select the same character in two distinct positions, mix a letter and a digit, then shrink two positions to one and expand again. The second choice must have been removed and be required again. Check the cart, order, receipt and kitchen ticket: positions remain distinct, without addition/removal signs or another charge. The absolute format price is counted once; only modifiers add their configured deltas. If refused, reload the item and check its role, source, active choices and position counts. Remove dependent conditions before deleting their source. A source belonging to another item or restaurant, a cycle, an invalid character or two choices in one position is rejected; invalid saves must not partially apply variant changes. Choose a variant on mobile On the updated handheld POS, a new item opens its outstanding choices directly. A valid single choice advances to the next group, including optional toppings; use Next or Done to finish a multiple-choice group. The Add/Extra/No palette appears only when the group enables Use conversational modifiers in POS, on both mobile and iPad. Otherwise only the values appear. With the palette enabled, choose the verb and then the ingredient; chips show the selected combinations. This group option is separate from the item’s quick-entry setting. The top handle or panel close button returns to the summary without losing choices. An incomplete required group blocks Next or Done. Review the blue values, quantity and note, then tap Add. Reopening a field from the summary does not restart the whole sequence. Items configured for quick entry retain that policy and conditional groups remain validated. Variant prices remain absolute and modifier prices remain deltas. group setting and refresh. Browse the library on mobile On a handheld terminal, open Library. The filter button selects Items, Combos or Discounts. Under Items, choose a category in the selector above the list, search for a product and tap its row to open the existing editor. Price and availability remain visible, with a separate switch for authorized users. This internal list does not change published menu groups, ingredients, portions or variant rules configured in Admin.

articles.title: Restaurant calendar and exceptions
articles.description: Admin → Restaurant calendar
articles.body: Admin → Restaurant calendar Inspect a date Select the calendar period and the relevant service/date. Review the scheduled entries and restaurant timezone before making an exception. Add or edit an exception Use the date’s offered exception controls, set the affected service/hours and save. Review the calendar result and the corresponding guest availability. Remove an obsolete exception Review the affected date before removing an exception. Confirm that normal scheduling now applies; existing orders still need individual review if their fulfillment changed.

articles.title: Seats, courses, hold and fire
articles.description: Open the active table bill. Course availability depends on the restaurant’s POS profile and deployed API capabilities.
articles.body: Open the active table bill. Course availability depends on the restaurant’s POS profile and deployed API capabilities. Availability and access Advanced actions appear only when the installed POS and API advertise the required capability and your role permits them. Refresh a changed bill before retrying; never create another charge to resolve an uncertain result. Keep kitchen release separate from cash collection Holding or firing a course changes kitchen timing, not payment status. A table may be served before collection; do not count it as cash until the money is received and confirmed on an enrolled POS with an open drawer session. A pending cash payment must be resolved before closing the drawer. The card terminal deposit is a separate end-of-day action. Assign seats and courses Before sending, assign items to Table or selected guests and choose their course. Check course order and required item options. Financial seat allocation can later change without rewriting already-sent kitchen seating. Course management must be enabled in the device’s assigned shared mode; there is no independent iPad override. With a newly selected onsite method, the first course starts the empty draft; an explicit Immediate send choice is not reset by confirming the same method or refreshing settings. Items whose internal library category is configured for immediate sending enter Immediate send; menu display groups do not define this routing. Send is still required: adding an item never fires or prints it automatically. Refresh retains selected courses and holds that remain valid. Disabling course management stops assigning courses to new items; saved kitchen history is not rewritten. After a confirmed reset, the next check gets its own initial course and does not inherit holds or pending fires from the previous check. With compatible API and POS versions, editing a saved item’s places follows the same device-assigned mode as the initial send. Optional seats permits Table; Required seats requires a numbered place when covers are defined. Check the assigned mode and refresh its settings if the choice is rejected. Keep the item in its editor and reopen the correct check if the service has changed; do not resend food to correct its place. The API correction must be released before the POS that supplies this context: updating only one side does not guarantee this behavior. Hold or fire a course Review the held course and use Fire to release the selected eligible food. Shared physical units launch once even when their price is split. Refresh after uncertainty rather than sending the same food as a new sale. A historical shared batch can block a partial release. Repeat food as a new sale Where Repeat is offered, review the copied food in the provisional cart and send through normal validation. The action does not copy a fractional charge or previous offering into a new payment. Stock changes only through the normal new-order flow. Control courses on mobile On the updated mobile POS, the bottom Menu strip selects the course for the next items. In Check, each course retains its state and controls: fire to release, stop to hold and ⋯ for other permitted actions. Buttons are separate and compact; selecting the active course does not send it. Send at the top uses the existing Foody workflow and pending release selections. A course shared across bills retains one physical production. Permissions, timing, submitted states and repeat restrictions still apply.

articles.title: Discount, comp and void
articles.description: Select the item or bill and open its available Actions/Options. Check whether it is a draft, sent food or a saved financial share.
articles.body: Select the item or bill and open its available Actions/Options. Check whether it is a draft, sent food or a saved financial share. A paid takeaway being prepared remains active. POS Orders → All can also locate saved orders across sources and payment states; its details are read-only, not an adjustment or refund action. A missing kitchen print is not a reason to void food or collect payment again; verify the printer queue and profile first. Availability and access Advanced actions appear only when the installed POS and API advertise the required capability and your role permits them. Refresh a changed bill before retrying; never create another charge to resolve an uncertain result. Keep viewed QR order lines unchanged In Menu opened from a saved QR or web order, selected lines and the catalogue are viewable without adding, discounting, comping or voiding an item in this view. Other QR orders retain their IDs and payments. For an eligible operation on the live table check, use View table and verify the session and chosen bill; normal permissions and reasons still apply. Navigation never makes paid food editable and never refunds a payment. See order navigation. Read-only historical orders Opening a linked order from Transactions shows saved order details only. It does not offer comp, void or refund actions. Make changes through an eligible live check with the required permission; a food void is not a payment refund. Apply a reduction Choose an allowed library or manual amount/percentage discount, its scope and any required reason. Review the resulting total before saving. An item reduction and a whole-cart reduction have different bases; online promotion codes are separate. A source check-level discount must be explicitly removed before changing an unassigned sale to a saved onsite destination. The destination keeps and recalculates its own discount policy on new lines; saved lines and adjustments are not resubmitted by this handoff. Offer or undo an offering Choose Comp/Offer and the required reason, then review the title and scope before confirming. On the terminal, the panel identifies the affected item or check and explains the offering’s scope. Offering changes the charged amount, not food already prepared. Fees remain subject to restaurant policy; the title alone does not establish a zero balance. On a saved split line, only the selected eligible share is affected. The server checks permissions and reason and journals the adjustment. An offering does not automatically close a real check or record payment. Removing it requires permission and restores its recorded amount. Cancel food with a reason Use Void only for eligible unpaid food and supply its reason. Prepared/completed food or a paid/claimed fraction can prevent cancellation. For sent food, verify the cancellation result and kitchen ticket rather than deleting a draft line. Void is not a payment refund. Wait for counter card payment before kitchen preparation For a new counter pickup order paid by card, choose Pay, then Pay by card. Wait for terminal approval and for Foody to record the payment before preparation and the kitchen ticket start. During collection the payment remains pending and is excluded from the live order board. After a refusal or cancellation, keep the same checkout and retry there; do not send it to the kitchen to bypass payment. If approval succeeded but synchronization failed, reconcile the existing payment before starting another charge. Orders deliberately sent for table service before collection keep their existing send-then-pay flow. Any staged discounts and offered items remain part of the server-priced total used for this same charge. Check conditional item choices An item configured with repeated positions requires one separate choice per position according to the selected format. For example, a two-character Number Cake accepts 11, AB or A7. The format price replaces the base price; modifiers add only their configured surcharges. Reducing the position count removes newly hidden choices. Positions remain distinct in the cart, orders and kitchen ticket; review them before confirming. These customizations do not change delivery, availability, recipe, discount or cancellation rules. Configuration requires compatible versions and menu editing permission. See Variants and sizes for setup and recovery after a rejected selection. Access item options on mobile On the updated mobile POS, open the line and use ⋯ at the top of the item summary for permitted options, including Comp or Delete for an eligible draft. Existing reasons and permissions still apply. Done closes the panel and returns to the summary. Whole-check discounts and operations remain under Actions. The presentation change does not make sent lines editable or enable refunds.

articles.title: Managing Orders
articles.description: Every order from web, QR and POS in one live list. Track status, accept, send to the kitchen, and follow an order through to completion.
articles.body: Open the corresponding Foody workspace described below. The cross-channel All view on the POS requires compatible POS and API versions; updating the API alone does not update the installed POS. Open an order in Menu without merging QR payments On the updated POS, with orders.manage, tap an active or scheduled order in Orders, or a still-actionable order in All. An open manual check resumes its existing workspace; a QR, web or standalone order opens Menu with its own saved lines, number, statuses and total in the check panel. On a phone this panel fills the screen. The frame, Check, Actions and Guest tabs, item cards and totals use the standard Menu presentation without an extra back toolbar. Return to the list through Orders in the main navigation on tablets, or More → Orders on the handheld; Refresh and this order’s statuses are in Actions. Browsing the catalogue changes neither that order nor a retained draft. Actions → Manage this order offers eligible actions for that number only; collection also requires payments.manage. Opening the view never pays, dispatches or prints. Several QR guests at one table retain their individual orders and payments even within one table session. To add food or consult the table check, choose View table: only the same still-open session is eligible. If it contains separate bills, explicitly choose the bill. This navigation never merges or settles QR orders and never closes the table. An old session cannot open the next party’s service; pending financial actions must be resolved first. Completed, cancelled or refunded orders and read-only access retain historical viewing without reopening a sale. A paid order still being prepared remains viewable and actionable without another payment. If loading fails, use Retry rather than recreating the order. Install a compatible POS build to use this navigation. Manual orders from previous or unidentified table sessions stay separate by number; see previous services. Open the order behind a transaction In POS Transactions, select a confirmed payment and open a linked order to view its saved details in read-only mode. A single payment may cover multiple orders, and one order may have multiple payments. If the order cannot be loaded, retry later; do not assume that the payment failed or initiate a duplicate charge. Refund or void a Verifone online payment The Admin order payment section supports total or partial matched refunds and total VOID for an eligible single Verifone online payment, for owners/managers with payments.manage. Provider state, captured amount and verified history govern eligibility, not a fixed 24-hour rule. This does not cancel preparation or fulfillment and does not add a POS terminal refund button. Unknown results stay reserved and must be checked, never resubmitted. Invoice4U credit/cancellation documents require a separate check. See the online payment procedure. A captured ABS sale still AUTHORISED/AUTHORIZED or SETTLEMENT REQUESTED is not settled: Admin shows Available to void and only Void entire payment, with no prior refund. Refund payment and Available to refund require an explicit settled state or verified partially-refunded history. Generic APPROVED/COMPLETED, contradictory states or missing evidence offer neither action. A state change before confirmation rejects the stale action; it never switches VOID to REFUND automatically. Request rejected by Verifone means no return of funds is confirmed, not necessarily an issuer decline. Review the by-weight authorization ceiling For online by-weight orders, open Settings → Payments & VAT with settings.edit. Set Weight hold buffer % from 0 to 100 and save; the default for new restaurants is 20. A failed save keeps the draft. Zero still authorizes the estimate. Only the weight-priced subtotal gets a margin: 100 weighted + 50 fixed at 20% authorizes 170; delivery has no extra margin. Checkout shows the estimate, temporary ceiling and Confirm and authorize, in the restaurant theme. A changed ceiling requires customer review and another confirmation before payment; unknown policy blocks authorization. Existing reviewed checkouts and holds keep their ceiling. Staff confirm measured weights before capture and progression; excess beyond the hold is flagged for a separate payment, never automatically charged. Cash/pay-later makes no hold promise. Requires a configured authorize/capture provider, with partial capture, release and expiry validated before production. This neither changes the catering deposit/balance policy nor enables new-card saving with a CST weighted hold. What Is It? The Orders screen is one live list of every order — whether it came from the guest web app, a QR table, or the POS. From here you track status, accept orders, and send them to the kitchen. How It Works (Simply) - POS Orders → All reads saved orders across all sources and payment states. Active, Scheduled and Completed remain separate operational views. - Admin Orders → All uses the same restaurant-owned records; its selected dates and filters still apply. - Payment and preparation are independent: a paid takeaway being prepared remains active. - On a compatible POS, authorized actionable orders open in Menu; completed records remain historical. See saved-order navigation. Order flow 1. Placed — a paid web/QR order, or a POS order, arrives. 2. Accepted — you accept it (or it auto-accepts, depending on your workflow settings). 3. In kitchen — sent to preparation; a kitchen ticket can print automatically. 4. Ready / Completed — handed to the customer. Tip: workflow behavior (auto-accept, auto-send-to-kitchen, auto-print) is configured in Settings . See Workflow settings. Good to know - A prepaid-channel order awaiting payment remains consultable in All. Visibility is not payment approval and does not send food to the kitchen or print a ticket. - Unsaved local carts are not shared orders. Restaurant access and permissions still apply. - If a dish sold out while the customer was ordering, checkout blocks it — see Availability. Review the WhatsApp attachment In an order, the preview of a configured Meta photo/PDF message shows the filename and Preview attachment. This opens the authorized fixed file or the PDF generated for that order without sending a message. If the file or amounts change after review, prepare a fresh preview before sending. Customer messages retains the filename with each attempt, including failures; Delivered and Read come from WhatsApp’s return. A filename alone does not prove delivery. The binding is configured in Order workflow or Communications → WhatsApp. Review a route-based delivery reminder For an assigned delivery with a saved customer-window setting, reminders use the route arrival plus the configured duration, rather than the order’s broad scheduled slot. For example, arrival at 08:30 and 90 minutes produces 08:30–10:00. Configure it in Orders → Deliveries → allocation, beside the time at each stop, and review the manual or approved WhatsApp preview before sending. The same range supplies Twilio, Meta and stage reminders; existing template variables and J-1 eligibility remain in effect. Unconfigured historic routes keep the original saved slot. If the range cannot be verified, recalculate the route and reopen the reminder. A changed approved preview must be reviewed again before sending. Editing a template alone does not calculate a route or change its margin. Add items from the article library With orders.manage access, open New order. Select a carte or Article library above the search field. The library includes all active restaurant items, including items outside any menu or the selected rotating series, and is available even when there is no POS carte. Search by item name and select an item; choose its size, modifiers or combo contents when prompted. Sold-out items remain disabled and inactive items are absent. Switching between a carte and the library preserves the ticket. Complete contact and fulfillment details, review the total and submit once. Adding an item here does not publish it on a menu or the guest website. If an item is missing, check its active status in Items; for a sold-out item, check its stock and availability before retrying. Make a one-order combo exception With orders.manage permission, open New order or edit a saved order in Admin and open its combo composition. In the relevant step, select Choose another item. Remove one selected unit first if the step is full, search the restaurant article library and choose the replacement and its size. Exception · included identifies the choice. Active fixed-price individual items are eligible, including items outside the active carte; inactive, sold-out and weight-priced items and other combos cannot be used. Required step quantities, per-item limits and configured portions still apply. Save the combo, review the ticket and submit once. For example, replace the beef in a two-main Mamie formula with fish while retaining chicken. The replacement and its size add no surcharge; other normal configured choices keep their existing surcharges. The formula base price and saved definition do not change, and editing an existing order preserves its original base-price snapshot. The choice survives draft restoration and reopening the order editor. Guests cannot request this exception. If rejected, refresh availability and choose an active item in an allowed size; a failed saved-order replacement retains the previous composition. Wait for counter card payment before kitchen preparation For a new counter pickup order paid by card, choose Pay, then Pay by card. Wait for terminal approval and for Foody to record the payment before preparation and the kitchen ticket start. During collection the payment remains pending and is excluded from the live order board. After a refusal or cancellation, keep the same checkout and retry there; do not send it to the kitchen to bypass payment. If approval succeeded but synchronization failed, reconcile the existing payment before starting another charge. Orders deliberately sent for table service before collection keep their existing send-then-pay flow. Understand series stock after order edits Predefined item stocks now have a journal under Items & menus → Stock history and on each product. A rotating carte can prepare initial allowances per series and publish them without restoring already committed units. Previous remaining counts are not carried forward. Order changes and pre-production releases use the original frozen pool; a produced item remains consumed. Ingredient/preparation quantities and recipe costs remain separate. See Availability for initial imports, corrections and history filters. Choose how to send a reminder Approved WhatsApp reminders can be previewed early, while manual buttons remain blocked until the day before delivery in the restaurant’s timezone. Orders → Deliveries → WhatsApp reminders reviews and confirms reminders across every route on the selected date; WhatsApp customer and Send this reminder handle one customer. Messages use the saved route’s calculated arrival window and assigned courier. Manual buttons use the global reminder template; automatic stages retain their explicitly configured template and timing in Order workflow. For day-before-only sending, select that timing on the intended stage, for example Ready. Opening a preview enables no trigger. A previously submitted, uncertain or failed reminder is never sent again by another mode, even if its text or provider changes. Changes before sending require a refreshed preview. Acceptance does not prove delivery; consult Customer messages on the order. Preview text represents the current calculation, not an earlier stored message. Keep courier contact details current Courier assignments use the contact name and phone saved for this establishment in Staff → Edit contact details. Updating those fields also refreshes the courier information used by upcoming delivery reminders here. Completed deliveries keep their historical contact snapshot. A prepared WhatsApp preview with older contact details must be refreshed and reviewed before sending. The staff home address is not part of the customer reminder. Recover a delivery after a test departure Starting courier mode marks assigned orders Out for delivery. If this was a test departure, a user with order-management permission can open Orders → Deliveries, select the date and choose Undo departure while no arrival, delivery or skipped stop has been recorded. Out for delivery orders return to In preparation; the route returns to draft and can be unassigned and reallocated. This is a delivery correction, not a new order, refund or reprint. Payments and previously sent messages are preserved. See the dispatch procedure. Check conditional item choices An item configured with repeated positions requires one separate choice per position according to the selected format. For example, a two-character Number Cake accepts 11, AB or A7. The format price replaces the base price; modifiers add only their configured surcharges. Reducing the position count removes newly hidden choices. Positions remain distinct in the cart, orders and kitchen ticket; review them before confirming. These customizations do not change delivery, availability, recipe, discount or cancellation rules. Configuration requires compatible versions and menu editing permission. See Variants and sizes for setup and recovery after a rejected selection. Track every saved order across POS and Admin Open POS → Orders → All, or Admin → Orders → All for the same restaurant. Counter, Admin-entered, website, QR and connected-channel orders share the existing order API; source and dine-in/pickup/delivery are independent filters. The POS All list has no default date, status, source, fulfillment-type or payment filter and loads more records as you scroll. Open a row for read-only items, totals, preparation and payment status. Switching back into All reloads it; pull down on a populated list to refresh, and retry a visible loading error instead of treating it as an empty history. Confirmed live order updates also refresh the retained list. Payment-pending web orders may require this read refresh because they do not emit a kitchen-arrival event. In Admin, widen the period and reset filters when searching for older orders. Do not recreate, recharge or reprint an order merely because it is absent from a filtered view. Mode selection and any customer prompt precede items in a new onsite sale. The table/check is chosen only at Send/Continue; cancellation preserves the source. See whole-check fulfillment. Private guest context is staff-only, never a public checkout answer or notification variable. Find a counter sale after payment A paid takeaway sale sent to the kitchen belongs in Orders → Active while food is being prepared, not Completed merely because payment succeeded. Open the correct takeaway filter and clear other filters if needed. Transactions records the collection separately and refreshes on entry. On the updated handheld, a confirmed recorded collection opens receipt choice, then New sale completes the flow explicitly. Tablets retain the brief Payment recorded confirmation and automatic return. Clearing the current POS bill does not delete the saved order; Orders → All remains available for cross-channel tracking. If paper is missing, verify the profile, current POS/printer association and printer history before reprinting or collecting any additional payment. See counter checkout. The Client tab uses the order's saved name/phone, not a guessed customer from another bill. Optional contact collection is configured per fulfillment method. Additional kitchen batches retain coherent contact details without sending a new order-created confirmation for each course; status notifications remain separate. Contact customers on WhatsApp With permission to manage orders, select one or more rows and choose Send a WhatsApp message . The page checkbox selects only displayed orders, up to 25; changing filters, date, page or restaurant clears the selection. The same composer is available in order details. Choose WhatsApp Business for the configured approved global confirmation, reminder or satisfaction model, or WhatsApp app for editable text per recipient. Review every phone and message. A Business batch confirms the ready count and produces one message per order; a customer with several orders may receive several messages. Unavailable previews, reminders that are not due and previous attempts are excluded. A changed order stops remaining sends until another review. Refresh checks existing attempts without automatically replaying an uncertain result. For app messages, open each conversation and send inside WhatsApp; Foody reports opening only. Automations keep their workflow configuration. See the WhatsApp guide for language, attachments, reminder requirements and recovery. Navigate a mobile sale In the updated mobile version, use Menu to add items, Check to review lines and courses, and Actions for check operations. The badge shows item quantity. The top button follows the permitted workflow action; on an empty check, View checks returns to the floor. Actions → Details → Guest displays saved contact information. See mobile order entry for this presentation. The Orders list and kitchen statuses remain independent of settlement. In the handheld Checks list, All checks and floor plans share one radio sheet. Filters retain authorized custom checks, groups and sections; Refresh reloads the data. Search matches visible names within the accessible scope, without opening another restaurant. Tables are grouped into Your checks and Other checks, followed by named checks. Closing a named check remains a separate confirmed action for authorized staff; a check with unsent items or an unpaid balance must not be closed merely to remove it from the list. Inside a menu group, use the single Back arrow to go up. Compact photo tiles keep the item name centered on up to two lines; iPad navigation and presentation retain their existing behavior. WhatsApp template image Approved WhatsApp Utility templates with a photo automatically use the image retrieved from Meta when no local file was selected. The preview displays that image; a change before a manual send requires another review. Retrieval failure blocks sending without a text-only fallback. Configure or refresh the template in Settings → Communications → WhatsApp. See the WhatsApp guide. Choose the customer WhatsApp recipient If the customer uses a different WhatsApp number, open Clients → their profile, select Use for WhatsApp under Phone numbers and save. That number is used by Meta and Twilio messages and by WhatsApp app handoffs from the order, including link and document sharing. The order phone remains its contact and SMS-verification number. Check the preview recipient; changing the WhatsApp selection requires a new reviewed preview before an API send. Saving the customer profile sends no test message. Open the current weekly batch automatically For a restaurant configured for weekly batches, open Home or Orders using the Série date basis. The current batch is selected by default even without orders; its totals then stay at zero. It advances after the previous batch’s final fulfillment day in the restaurant timezone, without waiting for the first order or for ordering to open. An open page follows this change on the next automatic refresh (about one minute) or when you return to the tab. You can select an older service in the calendar; that selection stays in place while the page is open. An order for a later week does not replace the current batch as the default. A payment-attention link keeps its explicit period. If the date looks incorrect, check the configured fulfillment days and restaurant timezone, then reload. Rollover does not create an order or publish a menu.

articles.title: Move, merge and transfer items
articles.description: Open the table bill or a saved item’s Options. Whole-bill movement and selected-item transfer are different actions.
articles.body: Open the table bill or a saved item’s Options. Whole-bill movement and selected-item transfer are different actions. Availability and access Advanced actions appear only when the installed POS and API advertise the required capability and your role permits them. Refresh a changed bill before retrying; never create another charge to resolve an uncertain result. Move a bill without duplicating cash Moving or merging a bill changes its table allocation, not the physical cash already counted in a drawer. If a payment is claimed or its result is uncertain, resolve that exact payment before moving the bill. Do not use a move, merge, or payment-method correction to turn a card result into a cash sale; cash collection is recorded only when money is received on an enrolled POS with an open drawer session. Move a bill Choose Move, select an authorized destination and read the confirmation before saving. Reopen the destination to verify the bill and covers. Moving a financial bill does not resend food to the kitchen. A payment in progress can block movement. This saved-bill operation is distinct from changing a draft's fulfillment method: the latter never merges into a financial check. Selecting a table with one refuses and cancels the pending draft transfer without changing its source; see changing a draft's service. Merge occupied table bills Choose the supported merge action and an authorized unpaid target, then review both totals/covers. The visible merged bill retains the original pricing policies and food history. Review its new balance before taking a single payment. Paid or actively claimed bills cannot be merged. Transfer saved items Open the saved item → Options → Move, choose an existing authorized table bill and confirm. A regular quantity line moves its quoted units; isolate one portion with Split first if needed. Covers stay with their bills; moved items begin at Table at the destination. Unsent drafts and named non-table tickets are outside this saved-table path. Kitchen history and stock are not duplicated. Select the check on the terminal On the updated handheld terminal, open Checks with the bottom receipt icon, then use the radio selector for All checks or the intended floor. A free table asks for covers when configured; an occupied table or named check opens its existing context. Verify the displayed table and bill before Actions → Move or an eligible transfer action. The view selector and floor panning neither move nor merge a bill: only confirmation of the actual business action can do so. Dismissing the selector without choosing changes no destination.

articles.title: Review and edit an order
articles.description: Admin → Orders → select an order
articles.body: Admin → Orders → select an order Availability and access Order changes require orders.manage; read access alone does not permit edits. Refund or void a Verifone online payment The Admin order payment section supports total or partial matched refunds and total VOID for an eligible single Verifone online payment, for owners/managers with payments.manage. Provider state, captured amount and verified history govern eligibility, not a fixed 24-hour rule. This does not cancel preparation or fulfillment and does not add a POS terminal refund button. Unknown results stay reserved and must be checked, never resubmitted. Invoice4U credit/cancellation documents require a separate check. See the online payment procedure. A captured ABS sale still AUTHORISED/AUTHORIZED or SETTLEMENT REQUESTED is not settled: Admin shows Available to void and only Void entire payment, with no prior refund. Refund payment and Available to refund require an explicit settled state or verified partially-refunded history. Generic APPROVED/COMPLETED, contradictory states or missing evidence offer neither action. A state change before confirmation rejects the stale action; it never switches VOID to REFUND automatically. Request rejected by Verifone means no return of funds is confirmed, not necessarily an issuer decline. Find the right order Choose order/date basis, status and fulfillment filters. Open the order and verify number, customer, service date and payment status before acting. Create a staff order Use New order, select items/options and fill the required contact and fulfillment fields. Review the total and submit once; check the created order before retrying an uncertain result. Edit saved details Use the available edit action to change customer, address or fulfillment details. Save and reread the order; review preparation, fees and date restrictions before changing an existing schedule. Accept, prepare and hand over Use only the next status actions offered for the order. Verify acceptance, kitchen, ready and handover results separately from payment. Check consequences before rejection or cancellation. Send customer messages deliberately In order details, Send a WhatsApp message opens the shared Business/app composer. Customer messages retains tracked attempts and provider evidence. Follow the detailed procedure below for one order or a selection. Review the WhatsApp attachment In an order, the preview of a configured Meta photo/PDF message shows the filename. Click it to open the authorized fixed file or the PDF generated for that order without sending a message. If the file or amounts change after review, prepare a fresh preview before sending. Customer messages retains the filename with each attempt, including failures; Delivered and Read come from WhatsApp’s return. A filename alone does not prove delivery. The binding is configured in Order workflow or Communications → WhatsApp. Add items from the article library With orders.manage access, open New order. Select a carte or Article library above the search field. The library includes all active restaurant items, including items outside any menu or the selected rotating series, and is available even when there is no POS carte. Search by item name and select an item; choose its size, modifiers or combo contents when prompted. Sold-out items remain disabled and inactive items are absent. Switching between a carte and the library preserves the ticket. Complete contact and fulfillment details, review the total and submit once. Adding an item here does not publish it on a menu or the guest website. If an item is missing, check its active status in Items; for a sold-out item, check its stock and availability before retrying. Review a route-based delivery reminder For an assigned delivery with a saved customer-window setting, reminders use the route arrival plus the configured duration, rather than the order’s broad scheduled slot. For example, arrival at 08:30 and 90 minutes produces 08:30–10:00. Configure it in Orders → Deliveries → allocation, beside the time at each stop, and review the manual or approved WhatsApp preview before sending. The same range supplies Twilio, Meta and stage reminders; existing template variables and J-1 eligibility remain in effect. Unconfigured historic routes keep the original saved slot. If the range cannot be verified, recalculate the route and reopen the reminder. A changed approved preview must be reviewed again before sending. Editing a template alone does not calculate a route or change its margin. Make a one-order combo exception With orders.manage permission, open New order or edit a saved order in Admin and open its combo composition. In the relevant step, select Choose another item. Remove one selected unit first if the step is full, search the restaurant article library and choose the replacement and its size. Exception · included identifies the choice. Active fixed-price individual items are eligible, including items outside the active carte; inactive, sold-out and weight-priced items and other combos cannot be used. Required step quantities, per-item limits and configured portions still apply. Save the combo, review the ticket and submit once. For example, replace the beef in a two-main Mamie formula with fish while retaining chicken. The replacement and its size add no surcharge; other normal configured choices keep their existing surcharges. The formula base price and saved definition do not change, and editing an existing order preserves its original base-price snapshot. The choice survives draft restoration and reopening the order editor. Guests cannot request this exception. If rejected, refresh availability and choose an active item in an allowed size; a failed saved-order replacement retains the previous composition. Find the original stock movement Predefined item stocks now have a journal under Items & menus → Stock history and on each product. A rotating carte can prepare initial allowances per series and publish them without restoring already committed units. Previous remaining counts are not carried forward. Order changes and pre-production releases use the original frozen pool; a produced item remains consumed. Ingredient/preparation quantities and recipe costs remain separate. See Availability for initial imports, corrections and history filters. Choose how to send a reminder Approved WhatsApp reminders can be previewed early, while manual buttons remain blocked until the day before delivery in the restaurant’s timezone. Orders → Deliveries → WhatsApp reminders reviews and confirms reminders across every route on the selected date; WhatsApp customer and Send this reminder handle one customer. Messages use the saved route’s calculated arrival window and assigned courier. Manual buttons use the global reminder template; automatic stages retain their explicitly configured template and timing in Order workflow. For day-before-only sending, select that timing on the intended stage, for example Ready. Opening a preview enables no trigger. A previously submitted, uncertain or failed reminder is never sent again by another mode, even if its text or provider changes. Changes before sending require a refreshed preview. Acceptance does not prove delivery; consult Customer messages on the order. Preview text represents the current calculation, not an earlier stored message. Keep the order’s variant positions When adding an item configured with positions, choose a character or option in every required field before Add to order. The format price is counted once. Order details list each position separately from additions/removals; quantity and note edits preserve these choices. Review them before confirmation and preparation. Send WhatsApp messages for one or several orders Prerequisites: permission to manage orders. Sending from Foody requires an already configured, active business number and approved model. Creating or editing models still requires settings access. 1. In order details, click Send a WhatsApp message beneath the customer’s contact details or in Actions . For several orders, select list rows and click the same button. Selection covers only the displayed page, up to 25 orders; changing filters, date, page or restaurant clears it. 2. Choose WhatsApp Business to send from Foody, or WhatsApp app to prepare editable text and send it yourself. 3. With Business, choose Order confirmation , Delivery reminder or Satisfaction after an order . Foody uses the configured approved global model, including its actual language and attachment. This panel cannot send free text through the API or choose an arbitrary library model. Select each recipient to check the phone, sender and exact content. Click an attachment’s filename to preview it. 4. Only ready previews can be sent. Missing details, reminders that are not due and previous attempts stay visible. Reminders retain their sending-date policy and need the saved delivery window and assigned courier; satisfaction requires a completed delivery or pickup order and active configuration. Click Send message or Send N messages . For multiple selected orders, confirm the eligible count. Each order produces a separate message; one customer with several orders may receive several messages. 5. In the app channel, choose confirmation, delivery information or receipt link. Language starts with the customer’s language, falling back to the restaurant’s language. Each draft and language can be edited. Open WhatsApp opens only the selected conversation; send inside WhatsApp, then return to select the next recipient. Foody reports only WhatsApp opened , without claiming sending or delivery. Discarding edited text requires confirmation. Result and recovery: Business statuses distinguish acceptance from delivery and reading when reported by the provider. Refresh checks the original attempt without resending it. A lost response remains unconfirmed and is never replayed automatically. If an order or model changes, remaining sends stop: refresh and review again. Correct missing saved details or configuration, then refresh unavailable previews. Allow pop-ups if the app does not open. Customer messages retains tracked history. Workflow automations keep their configured models and triggers; opening this panel does not activate or change them. WhatsApp template image Approved WhatsApp Utility templates with a photo automatically use the image retrieved from Meta when no local file was selected. The preview displays that image; a change before a manual send requires another review. Retrieval failure blocks sending without a text-only fallback. Configure or refresh the template in Settings → Communications → WhatsApp. See the WhatsApp guide. Choose the customer WhatsApp recipient If the customer uses a different WhatsApp number, open Clients → their profile, select Use for WhatsApp under Phone numbers and save. That number is used by Meta and Twilio messages and by WhatsApp app handoffs from the order, including link and document sharing. The order phone remains its contact and SMS-verification number. Check the preview recipient; changing the WhatsApp selection requires a new reviewed preview before an API send. Saving the customer profile sends no test message.

articles.title: Order types and fulfillment
articles.description: Foody supports dine-in, pickup, delivery, and scheduled orders. Learn what each means and how to enable them.
articles.body: Admin → Settings → Orders / POS → order entry. Tableless dine-in, whole-check method selection and optional customer prompts require compatible POS and API versions. Their Admin configuration also requires a compatible Admin version; an API update does not update either client. Collect cash for a POS order type Dine-in and counter pickup orders can be collected in cash only on an enrolled POS with an open cash drawer session. Open More → Reports → Cash drawer balance before taking the first cash payment, then settle the intended order or financial bill. A delivery or online pay-later order is not a recorded cash sale merely because cash is its intended tender; record only cash actually received. Card terminal deposits remain separate. Review the by-weight authorization ceiling For online by-weight orders, open Settings → Payments & VAT with settings.edit. Set Weight hold buffer % from 0 to 100 and save; the default for new restaurants is 20. A failed save keeps the draft. Zero still authorizes the estimate. Only the weight-priced subtotal gets a margin: 100 weighted + 50 fixed at 20% authorizes 170; delivery has no extra margin. Checkout shows the estimate, temporary ceiling and Confirm and authorize, in the restaurant theme. A changed ceiling requires customer review and another confirmation before payment; unknown policy blocks authorization. Existing reviewed checkouts and holds keep their ceiling. Staff confirm measured weights before capture and progression; excess beyond the hold is flagged for a separate payment, never automatically charged. Cash/pay-later makes no hold promise. Requires a configured authorize/capture provider, with partial capture, release and expiry validated before production. This neither changes the catering deposit/balance policy nor enables new-card saving with a CST weighted hold. Dine-in and tables Dine-in describes onsite consumption, not a required table number.
